articles.title: Why the Jalen Hurts optimism feels forced amid Eagles offensive rebuild
articles.standfirst: Sean Mannion’s new system is bringing Hurts’ mobility back into focus
articles.summary: Sean Mannion’s new system is bringing Hurts’ mobility back into focus
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles didn't need another reminder of how badly their offense lost its rhythm last season. What they needed was evidence that the reset under Sean Mannion could unlock something that had gradually disappeared.

So far, Jalen Hurts is providing it. The quarterback has been one of the most talked-about players in Eagles camp, with coaches and teammates repeatedly pointing to the same thing, he looks quicker.

Hurts ’ rushing production declined sharply in 2025, when he finished with 421 yards and eight touchdowns on the ground, his lowest totals as Philadelphia’s full-time starter.

His designed-run usage also dropped substantially compared with earlier seasons. Mannion appears willing to change that.

The first-year offensive coordinator has incorporated more designed quarterback runs during camp while also introducing a more under-center-heavy structure, creating the possibility that Hurts could become a more active part of the rushing attack again.

Eagles defense notices Hurts’ speed

The strongest endorsement has come from the players tasked with chasing him.

“I think Jalen’s having a good camp,” defensive coordinator Vic Fangio said. “I think he looks faster.”

Fangio acknowledged that practice rules make judging sacks difficult because defenders cannot hit the quarterback, but he has seen several plays where the defense thought Hurts was trapped before he escaped.

“I think there’s been a few times where our guys think they had him and they really didn’t,” Fangio said.

Defensive tackle Jalen Carter offered an even more striking description.

“I don’t know what it is but when I’m watching and I’m running [after him], it’s like a movie, it feels like I’m going slow,” Carter said. “He be moving man, he’s been working hard and he’s the one, for sure.”

Hurts himself has resisted the idea that anything dramatic has changed physically, saying he does not “feel any different” from previous years. The offense around him, however, certainly does.

Sean Mannion asking Hurts to play faster

Hurts has emphasized that the new system still comes back to basic quarterback discipline.

“In the end, you're still playing the position, and you want to play the position the same way, play with your feet, sweep through your reads, know exactly where you're supposed to go with the ball,” Hurts said.

He added that the objective is to understand “what we're trying to attack, being on the same page and playing each play.”

That may be the most important difference after Philadelphia’s offense struggled to consistently find answers in 2025.

Mannion isn't simply asking Hurts to run more. He's trying to marry his mobility with quicker processing, cleaner footwork and a structure that can threaten defenses in several ways.

The Eagles still have high-end talent around him, including Saquon Barkley and DeVonta Smith . Yet Hurts remains the player capable of changing the ceiling of the entire unit.

If the version teammates are seeing in camp carries into the regular season, Philadelphia may not just have a refreshed offense. It may have rediscovered the quarterback who once made it so difficult to defend.

articles.title: Jalen Hurts POV Cam shows just how difficult playing quarterback in NFL is
articles.standfirst: The Philadelphia Eagles showcased to fans what playing QB against an NFL defense is like.
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Eagles showcased to fans what playing QB against an NFL defense is like.
articles.body:
By this point, it's practically known by everyone just how hard it is to play quarterback at a high level. Despite that, every NFL season comes and goes, and professional QBs are still criticized week-in, week-out .

That's the nature of playing such a high-profile position, and getting paid lots of money to do it. But there's a reason the very best quarterback get paid so much: It's one of the hardest jobs in all of sports . POV cams in the past have amplified that notion, with Tua Tagovailoa 's version with the Miami Dolphins going viral a couple of years ago.

Playing quarterback is way harder than many make it look on TV

Now, the Philadelphia Eagles have given fans an up-close look at what their quarterback, Jalen Hurts , has to go through on a per-snap basis. Making that particular play even more difficult was that it came from close to the goal line, so defenders and pass-catchers were more condensed.

Hurts was able to progress through his reads and find a pass-catcher for a touchdown . Still, it left many fans baffled at how he was even able to sit in the pocket and find his receiver.

" I don’t think people realize how hard it is to be a QB lol "

" Genuinely how tf do quarterbacks ever complete a pass "

" Genuinely this is so funny because people think playing QB isn’t one of the hardest things in the world and then you see an actual POV of a QB and it’s f**king impossible lol "

Hurts has one of the better offensive lines around the league, too, so fans can only imagine what it looks like from the pocket for a quarterback behind a bad offensive line.

articles.title: Saquon Barkley could return to MVP form, and that’s bad news for the NFC East
articles.standfirst: Saquon Barkley is back? The NFC East could be in trouble.
articles.summary: Saquon Barkley is back? The NFC East could be in trouble.
articles.body:
After delivering what was arguably the best individual season by a running back in NFL history in 2024, Saquon Barkley saw his production decline in 2025, just like the Philadelphia Eagles , who were unable to replicate the dominance they displayed the previous year.

However, “coming back down to earth” for Barkley still meant finishing with 1,140 rushing yards , the fourth-best mark of his career. The difference was that, after becoming a constant threat with explosive 30, 40, and even 50-plus-yard runs during his first season in Philadelphia , things became much more difficult for the star running back in his second year with the team.

Barkley went from recording 11 games with more than 100 rushing yards in 2024 to just three in 2025 , raising questions about whether he could return to the level that made him one of the league’s most dominant players.

The biggest question is whether the 29-year-old running back has reached the point that many veteran players at the position eventually face: a physical decline that prevents them from replicating historic seasons. But according to Lane Johnson , there is still plenty left to expect from Barkley.

During Wednesday’s Eagles practice, the veteran offensive lineman made it clear that fans should not count out the No. 26 and predicted a version of Barkley much closer to the one that dominated in 2024 .

Lane Johnson believes in Saquon Barkley’s resurgence

“The more productive we are in the run game and stuff feeds off that, we'll see the Saquon from two years ago. We'll see the big plays, we'll see him flex wide at wide receiver, we'll see him in the screen game,” Johnson said via The Athletic’s Zach Berman .

Although Barkley is entering his ninth NFL season, his workload is not comparable to many running backs his age. The three-time Pro Bowler has played only 113 career games after missing most of the 2020 season due to injury and appearing in just seven playoff games during his time with the New York Giants because of the team’s struggles to reach the postseason.

Even though Barkley’s career is entering an advanced stage for a running back, Johnson believes he still has plenty left in the tank. And if he is right, Eagles fans could once again see the explosive version of the player who dominated the NFL in 2024 .

articles.title: Kylie Kelce liked Jason treating her like an object at the gym… What does she mean by that?
articles.standfirst: A simple request for workout advice turned into a flirty exchange between the couple
articles.summary: A simple request for workout advice turned into a flirty exchange between the couple
articles.body:
There are plenty of reasons married couples choose not to work out together. In the Kelce household, one of them apparently involves Jason Kelce being unable to focus.

Kylie Kelce opened up about the couple’s gym dynamic during an appearance on Ilona Maher’s new workout series Power Hour, explaining that her retired NFL husband isn't exactly the person she turns to when she wants serious feedback.

Asked whether she and Jason train together, Kylie didn't hesitate: “God, no. I don’t hate myself that much,” she joked.

She then explained that they have worked out together in their garage before, including one session in which she was performing Romanian deadlifts and wanted Jason to check her technique.

“After a minute of me doing it, I was like, ‘Critique my form’,” Kylie recalled. “And he was like, ‘I’m gonna be honest, I’m really distracted.’ And I was like, ‘You’re useless’.”

Kylie not offended by the attention

Maher quickly picked up on what had distracted the former Philadelphia Eagles center and suggested Kylie might need a more neutral training partner.

“You’ve gotta get a third party who’s not gonna objectify you,” Maher joked. “That’s tough to have somebody objectifying you like that in the gym.”

Kylie’s response made clear that she was not particularly bothered: “I actually kind of liked it,” she said with a grin.

The conversation then shifted to whether the attraction goes both ways, and Kylie was equally direct when Maher asked if she objectifies her husband: “1000%, I do,” she replied.

“Because it’s all about equality,” Maher joked. “We’re feminists,” with Kylie replying: “Thank you. Yeah, we’re feminists. Have you seen his shoulders?”

Flirting part of Jason and Kylie’s marriage

The exchange fits with how Kylie has previously described her relationship with Jason. The couple met on Tinder and married in 2018. They now have four daughters, Wyatt, Elliotte, Bennett and Finn .

Earlier this year, Kylie said on her Not Gonna Lie podcast that she expects the flirting to continue even after years of marriage and the demands of raising a family.

“I actually give my husband s**t if he walks past me in the kitchen, doesn’t, like, grab my ass,” she said. “Flirt with me. Imma flirt with you. You better flirt with me.”

That makes the gym story less of an isolated joke and more of a glimpse into the way the couple has kept a playful dynamic alive.

Jason may not be much help when it comes to critiquing Kylie ’s deadlift form. Judging by her reaction, though, she doesn't seem especially interested in fixing that particular problem.

articles.title: A.J. Brown gives Jalen Hurts cold shoulder in heated Patriots-Eagles reunion
articles.standfirst: The former Eagles stars embraced and spoke privately after Thursday’s joint practice
articles.summary: The former Eagles stars embraced and spoke privately after Thursday’s joint practice
articles.body:
The most telling moment of A.J. Brown ’s first week working opposite the Philadelphia Eagles didn't come during a route, a touchdown or a competitive rep. It came after practice, when he turned around, headed back toward his former teammates and sought out Jalen Hurts .

The two embraced, spoke privately for several minutes and then dapped each other up before leaving the field Thursday, according to multiple reporters covering the joint session between the New England Patriots and Eagles.

It mattered because Brown had acknowledged only a day earlier that he and Hurts hadn't spoken since Philadelphia traded him to New England in June.

Their public comments had already hinted there was no open hostility. Brown said there was still love on his side, while Hurts made clear that his affection for his former teammate had not disappeared.

The post-practice conversation gave those words more weight.

Brown and Hurts more than routine quarterback-receiver pairing

During four seasons together, Brown and Hurts became one of the defining offensive partnerships in Philadelphia.

They helped the Eagles reach two Super Bowls, win one championship and produce some of the strongest offensive seasons in franchise history.

Their relationship also extended beyond football, with Hurts serving as the godfather to Brown ’s daughter. That history is why the silence following the trade drew attention.

The joint practices this week marked the first time the two had been placed on opposite sides, and Brown made himself visible against his former defense with several touchdowns during competitive periods.

Yet the most significant development may have been what happened once the work ended.

Both players trying to move forward

Brown ’s final stretch in Philadelphia wasn't especially smooth.

He finished the Eagles ’ playoff loss to the San Francisco 49ers with three catches for 25 yards on seven targets, dropped two passes and had a heated sideline exchange with head coach Nick Sirianni .

His move to New England gave him a fresh start and reunited him with Mike Vrabel , who previously coached him with the Tennessee Titans.

Hurts , meanwhile, is adapting to another offensive reset. Sean Mannion is now calling plays, continuing a pattern of coordinator changes throughout the quarterback’s career.

“Jalen's been awesome,” Mannion said. “I really think he can do anything we ask of him.” The football consequences of Brown ’s departure will take much longer to evaluate.

The personal story appears clearer. After weeks of questions about whether the relationship had gone cold, Brown and Hurts finally spoke face to face.

articles.title: Dean Blandino reveals Taylor Swift's frustration with famous tactic Eagles used to stop Chiefs
articles.standfirst: A conversation about the NFL’s tush push helped create a friendship with the global superstar
articles.summary: A conversation about the NFL’s tush push helped create a friendship with the global superstar
articles.body:
T aylor Swift ’s connection to the NFL has mostly been defined by her support of Travis Kelce and the Kansas City Chiefs , but Dean Blandino has revealed the singer also has strong opinions about one of the league’s biggest debates.

The former NFL vice president of officiating said Swift unexpectedly approached him after a Chiefs-Eagles matchup and immediately shared her thoughts on Philadelphia’s controversial “tush push” play.

Blandino , who now works as a rules analyst for FOX Sports, said the conversation happened at Patrick Mahomes ’ birthday party last September after Kansas City faced Philadelphia. What started as a football discussion eventually turned into a friendship with Swift and Kelce .

“We did a game in Kansas City last year. This person came up to me, gave me a big hug, and said that she agreed that the tush push sucks, and it was Taylor Swift, and we just hit it off and became friends,” Blandino said on the House of Haymaker podcast.

The meeting later led to Blandino receiving an invitation to Swift and Kelce ’s wedding at Madison Square Garden, where around 1,000 guests attended the July ceremony.

Taylor Swift joins debate over Eagles’ signature play

The “tush push” has become one of the NFL’s most talked-about strategies since the Philadelphia Eagles turned it into a near-automatic short-yardage weapon.

The play involves teammates pushing quarterback Jalen Hurts from behind to help gain extra yards, especially in situations where Philadelphia needs a first down or touchdown. While the Eagles have found tremendous success with the formation, it has also attracted criticism from fans, analysts, and opponents who believe the tactic should be reviewed or banned.

Swift ’s reported reaction puts her among those who have questioned the play, although she has not publicly called for the NFL to eliminate it.

Her opinion also carries an interesting connection because of her history with Philadelphia. Swift has performed at Lincoln Financial Field and has reportedly supported improvements at the stadium, including changes made around her Eras Tour appearance.

However, since beginning her relationship with Kelce , her NFL loyalty has shifted toward Kansas City, making the Eagles a natural rival from a football perspective.

The Chiefs and Eagles aren't scheduled to meet during the regular season, meaning Swift may only have to watch the tush push again if the teams meet in a future playoff matchup.

Blandino explains how unlikely friendship began

Blandino ’s story highlights another side of Swift ’s growing connection to football. While she has become one of the NFL’s most visible celebrities, the conversation showed her willingness to engage with the sport beyond simply supporting Kelce .

Since joining FOX Sports in 2017, Blandino has become a familiar face for NFL fans, breaking down complicated rules decisions and explaining controversial officiating calls.

His relationship with Swift developed from a simple football conversation, with the former official saying the two “hit it off” after discovering they shared the same view on the Eagles ’ most famous play.

Swift has become a major part of the NFL conversation over the past two seasons, but Blandino ’s story offers a different perspective on her involvement. Away from the spotlight, she is also following the details of the game and forming opinions on the strategies that shape it.

And when it comes to the tush push, it appears Swift is firmly in the group that would rather see it disappear.

articles.title: Eagles star Ja'Quinden Jackson discharged the hospital following hard hit suffered against Patriots
articles.standfirst: Philadelphia running back avoided a serious injury after frightening opening kickoff collision
articles.summary: Philadelphia running back avoided a serious injury after frightening opening kickoff collision
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles received a major scare during their preseason matchup against the New England Patriots when running back Ja’Quinden Jackson was taken from the field in an ambulance following a violent collision on the opening kickoff.

Hours later, the team and Jackson ’s representatives provided a much more encouraging update. Jackson was injured while covering the kickoff and making a tackle on Patriots returner Lan Larison .

After the play ended, the 24-year-old running back remained motionless on the field, prompting medical staff from both teams to rush over as players from both sidelines gathered in concern.

The Eagles announced that Jackson had movement and strength in all four extremities before he was transported to a local hospital for further evaluation. His agent, Damien Butler , later confirmed that Jackson was awake, alert and had received positive medical results.

“Ja’Quinden is awake, has full movement and use of all four limbs, and his CT scan came back negative,” Butler said in a statement.

“We are extremely grateful to the Philadelphia Eagles ’ medical staff and the first responders whose swift actions and exceptional care supported Ja’Quinden during this critical moment.”

Jackson was later released from the hospital and returned to Philadelphia with the Eagles .

Eagles teammates relieved after frightening scene

The emotional reaction from players highlighted how serious the moment appeared on the field. Eagles quarterback Tanner McKee said the team was immediately concerned after seeing Jackson remain down following the tackle.

“A lot of different emotions just praying and hoping that he’s OK,” McKee said. “Word was going around that he was talking, he was responsive and moving. That kind of got everybody to settle down a little bit and we know our teammate is doing OK.”

Head coach Nick Sirianni also admitted that watching the injury unfold was difficult for everyone involved.

“That’s always rough to see that,” Sirianni said. “I know our guys care about each other and so that’s tough. That’s tough… I’m glad he’s doing OK.”

Jackson ’s injury occurred less than a minute into the preseason contest, briefly stopping the game as medical personnel worked with him. He was placed on a stretcher and loaded into an ambulance, but he was seen raising his left arm as he was taken away from the field.

The injury came at a crucial time for Jackson , who signed with Philadelphia earlier this month after spending the 2025 season on the Jacksonville Jaguars ’ practice squad.

articles.title: Vic Fangio silences panic over Jalen Hurts' training camp interceptions
articles.standfirst: Jalen Hurts’ preseason struggles have raised some questions in Philadelphia, but Vic Fangio isn’t worried.
articles.summary: Jalen Hurts’ preseason struggles have raised some questions in Philadelphia, but Vic Fangio isn’t worried.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles are preparing to wrap up their preseason this Friday against the Cincinnati Bengals at Lincoln Financial Field , looking to regain momentum after losing their first two exhibition games against the Baltimore Ravens and the New England Patriots .

The team finished training camp on Wednesday with positive takeaways, especially regarding Jalen Hurts , who continues to adjust to new offensive coordinator Sean Mannion ’s system. While the quarterback is still becoming familiar with the scheme, the organization believes he will be ready for the start of the regular season.

One of the biggest concerns in recent weeks has been Hurts’ interceptions during practice. The quarterback threw at least five interceptions during the team’s two-day joint practices with the Patriots, raising some concerns around the reigning NFC champions.

However, defensive coordinator Vic Fangio dismissed any worries about the quarterback’s performance and said the mistakes are simply part of the adjustment process.

“He's learning a new offense. I think he's trying things, seeing what's available and what isn't available. So I don’t think that's gonna carry over,” Fangio said, as quoted by Eagles reporter Anthony DiBona .

Mannion’s arrival from the Green Bay Packers is aimed at revitalizing an offense that has lost some of its explosiveness in recent years, bringing new ideas, a different strategic approach, and a more modern system built around Hurts.

The quarterback, meanwhile, is looking to move past the disappointment of failing to repeat as champion last season and reestablish himself among the NFL’s elite. While an adjustment period is inevitable, the Eagles believe his talent will allow him to adapt quickly.

ESPN analyst Dan Graziano is also predicting a bounce-back season for Hurts and Philadelphia, arguing that the team has too much talent to suffer a major collapse.

“They’re too good to flop completely,” Graziano said.

articles.title: Who is Jackson O'Brien? Philadelphia Eagles' new gay cheerleader who has gone viral
articles.standfirst: The rookie cheerleader turned graduation day into double celebration
articles.summary: The rookie cheerleader turned graduation day into double celebration
articles.body:
Jackson O’Brien thought graduation day would already be one of the biggest moments of his life. Then, moments after walking across the stage, his phone delivered news that made the day even more unforgettable.

The Stockton University performing arts graduate had earned a place on the Philadelphia Eagles cheer team.

O’Brien , who is openly gay, immediately called his mother to tell her what had happened. The emotional exchange was captured on video and quickly went viral, drawing millions of views across social media.

“It was such a surreal moment, and with my friends all around me, it made it all the more special,” O’Brien said.

The Eagles later confirmed him as one of nine rookies on their 32-member cheer roster for the 2026 season.

The timing made the moment especially striking as one chapter was ending with his college graduation, and another was beginning almost immediately with a place in the NFL.

O’Brien reflects on his journey

The viral call was followed by a more personal message from O’Brien , who spoke openly about what dance has meant to him.

“If Jackson from last year saw where he is now, he would literally be like, ‘diva, you’re lying’. But I’m not! I’m not! I’m here!” he told followers.

“I will say until the day I die that dance saved my life. Now I have so many more people I get to dance for.”

O’Brien also thanked the people who supported him throughout the journey.

“To my friends and family who never let my light dim, thank you for being the glue what always keeps me together,” he wrote.

He added: “To represent one of the biggest sports teams in the country is an absolute dream, I feel so lucky to live this life.”

Eagles role offers O’Brien much bigger stage

O’Brien joins a Philadelphia squad that includes four male dancers for the upcoming season.

His arrival continues the broader growth of male cheerleaders across the NFL, with representation expanding significantly in recent years.

That visibility matters to O’Brien , but his immediate focus remains on performing and embracing the opportunity he worked toward.

“I just am so grateful for this moment and this opportunity,” he said. “And I can’t wait to keep showing up, showing who I am, and seeing all the support from everyone.”

O’Brien has already begun that next stage, making his Eagles cheerleading debut during the preseason at Lincoln Financial Field.

The viral video may have introduced him to millions of people, but the significance of the moment was much simpler.

He graduated from college, achieved one of his biggest professional goals and got to call his mother immediately afterward to tell her the dream had come true.

articles.title: Baby-faced Jason Kelce: Travis's brother breaks the internet with striking throwback photos from his days in Cincinnati
articles.standfirst: Jason Kelce's clean-shaven face has fans questioning whether it's really him
articles.summary: Jason Kelce's clean-shaven face has fans questioning whether it's really him
articles.body:
Jason Kelce has reminded fans that even the most recognizable celebrities can look completely different with one small change.

The retired Philadelphia Eagles center recently revisited photos from his University of Cincinnati football days, and his clean-shaven appearance left fans doing a double take.

The throwback images were shown during a recent episode of New Heights, the podcast Jason hosts with his younger brother, Kansas City Chiefs star Travis Kelce. Looking back at his younger self, Jason admitted that he doesn't particularly like the way his face looks without the beard that's become one of his most recognizable features.

“I just hate the way my face looks without a beard,” said Jason .

One photo showed Jason speaking to teammates during a Cincinnati practice, prompting him to question whether that was really what he looked like while shouting in a football huddle. The brothers then turned their attention to another surprising detail from Jason's college years: his eyebrows.

“That was back when I used to just take my razor, and that’s how I trim my eyebrows,” he said.

“I would just go straight across my eyebrows. So they ended up being super thin and not having any shape.”

Travis was clearly entertained by the revelation and agreed that his brother's eyebrows looked dramatically different from the ones he has today.

The discussion then shifted toward Travis ' own college grooming experiment. The Chiefs tight end recalled trying to shave his chest, only to discover that the hair seemed to grow back almost immediately. He eventually tried waxing instead, but that attempt went even worse.

Travis said the experience left his chest bloody and patchy, with scabs forming afterward. To the surprise of no-one, he decided to abandon the idea altogether.

Jason's beard has become part of the family

Jason's beard has become such an important part of his identity that even his family isn't accustomed to seeing him without it.

His wife, Kylie Kelce , previously joked on her podcast that she's never actually seen Jason's chin in person. She playfully speculated that there might be a cleft chin hiding underneath the beard, but said she'd never had the opportunity to find out.

Kylie also suggested that their four daughters could have a strong reaction if Jason suddenly shaved. According to her, the children have become so accustomed to seeing their father with facial hair that at least one of them might even cry if he appeared without it.

The college photographs show how much Jason's appearance has changed since his Cincinnati days. His younger, clean-shaven face looks almost unrecognizable compared with the heavily bearded personality fans came to know during his NFL career.

The brothers have also recently addressed another viral football moment involving Travis . Footage from Chiefs training camp showed him running a deliberately slow route, leading to widespread criticism and millions of views online.

Jason argued that practice should remain a place where players can experiment without worrying that every imperfect moment will be preserved on social media.

“I can’t stand when they put these clips online,” Jason said. “Can we just let practice be its own thing? We don’t need to show everything.”

Travis , meanwhile, explained that his slow pace was intentional and designed to tempt the defender into anticipating his move.

articles.title: The turf at the Eagles-Titans game reached 156,2 degrees: The cleats were melting!
articles.standfirst: With temperatures over 104 degrees, the players had to pour water on their cleats so the studs wouldn’t melt, while the Eagles coach needed an IV
articles.summary: With temperatures over 104 degrees, the players had to pour water on their cleats so the studs wouldn’t melt, while the Eagles coach needed an IV
articles.body:
Extreme temperatures continue to put world sport in check, and many athletes, coaches, and governing bodies are calling for changes to schedules and events to cope with the heat.

In recent weeks, for example, the organizers of LaVuelta were forced to shorten the stage between Palma del Rio and Cordoba (Spain) due to forecast temperatures that could reach 105,8º. But cases keep occurring.

In the NFL matchup between the Philadelphia Eagles and the Tennessee Titans , forecasts warned of temperatures close to 104º, with a higher heat index due to the humidity, so the authorities had issued an alert. But the artificial turf at the Nashville stadium reached a temperature of 156,2 degrees , causing the cleats on some players' shoes to begin to melt.

I had never stopped to think about how hot a stadium with artificial turf can get. The heat builds up and radiates back upward.

That forced the trainers to spray water on the soles to cool them down. "I had never stopped to think about how hot a stadium with artificial turf can get. The heat builds up and radiates upward," said Eagles player Jordan Mailata. "We have to fix this. That's why we want all fields to be natural grass, to establish a playing standard in the league where we don't put players in dangerous situations if it's not necessary."

Even Eagles coach Nick Sirianni needed an IV as a result of the extreme heat. “I didn’t play a single snap and they had to put me on an IV. I really appreciate the grit the players showed, because it wasn’t easy,” he said afterward.

"The break was like having a NASCAR pit crew help me get ready for the second half," said Cam Jurgens , who had to replace his cleats several times because they were melting. "That turf was radiating heat".

articles.title: Kelce Fatigue: NFL fans blame overexposure for backlash against Jason and Kylie’s new ad
articles.standfirst: Jason has become a common face on TV upon retiring from the NFL.
articles.summary: Jason has become a common face on TV upon retiring from the NFL.
articles.body:
Jason and Kylie Kelce have become fixtures of NFL coverage, but their latest television appearance is testing the patience of some fans, who say they are seeing the couple almost everywhere they look.

The pair headline a new NFL Sunday Ticket commercial built around a watch party at their home, with the lighthearted campaign quickly becoming a talking point for a very different reason.

The ad itself has not sparked much controversy, but its frequency has. NFL reporter James Palmer joked about the constant broadcasts, asking fans how many times they had seen the commercial.

“I'm looking for rough estimates,” Palmer wrote on X.com, formerly Twitter. “How many times do you think you've seen the Sunday Ticket commercial with the Kelce's nervous about their watch party? I'm ball parking my number around 34,531.”

And fans quickly joined the conversation, with one describing the situation as, “The Kelce overload.”

Another called the repeated exposure, “Total overkill. Hate it.”

And a third joked, “It's showing up in my dreams now.”

Others pushed back against the criticism, making clear that the commercial has its supporters as the reaction comes as Jason and Kylie continue to attract greater attention alongside Travis Kelce ’s relationship with Taylor Swift .

Travis even recently recalled how his nieces initially addressed Swift by her full name when they first met her as Jason then recalled the girls asking, “Taylor Swift, can I do this? Taylor Swift”, before adding, “You can call her Taylor.”

Jason backs up Eagles’ Jalen Hurts after Week 2 win

Jason also found himself defending Jalen Hurts after the Philadelphia Eagles ' Week 2 victory over the Tennessee Titans , following criticism of the quarterback's decision to slide on third down.

Drew Brees , who played previously for the New Orleans Saints and was calling the game alongside Adam Amin , questioned Hurts for coming up short as he felt the Super Bowl champion should have secured the first down.

“Lower your shoulder and go get the first down,” Brees said. “You slide they're going to mark the ball where you started the slide, not where you end the slide. So, it's not a Tush Push situation. It's not fourth and one. It's fourth and three."

But Kelce offered a different perspective shortly afterward, praising his former teammate as Hurts and the Eagles converted the fourth down, before eventually finding the end zone on the same possession.

“Playing quarterback pretty well,” Kelce wrote on X.com, defending Hurts after the star completed 26 of 37 passes for 264 yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions, whilst he also added 16 rushing yards.

But on an unfortunate note, Philadelphia dealt with injuries to Saquon Barkley and Dallas Goedert during the game, giving further context to the quarterback's cautious decision.

Barkley briefly left after suffering a stinger on the opening offensive play but returned in the third quarter. Goedert was not as fortunate, leaving with a right leg injury and will miss the following series of games.

articles.standfirst: Chicago faces Philadelphia at Soldier Field
articles.summary: Chicago faces Philadelphia at Soldier Field
articles.body:
Week 3 of the 2026-2027 NFL season brings a matchup with recent history and plenty at stake: the Chicago Bears host the Philadelphia Eagles at Soldier Field. On the home side, there is a hunger for revenge and the urgency to shake off a loss that left doubts; on the visitor's side, the feeling of a squad that keeps moving forward as what it is, a team used to winning.

It's one of those games that sets the tone for an entire month.

What time and where to watch the Eagles vs Bears game?

The game between Chicago and Philadelphia will be played at Soldier Field in Chicago, with kickoff scheduled for Monday, September 28, 2026, at 8:15 p.m. Eastern Time (7:15 p.m. Central Time and 5:15 a.m. Pacific Time).

Regarding the broadcast of this game, since it is part of the Monday night time slot, the natural point of reference is ESPN and ABC, along with their Spanish-language version, ESPN Deportes.

How do the Eagles and Bears arrive for Monday Night Football?

The Eagles started the campaign with a perfect record: 2-0, with wins over the Washington Commanders (24-22) and on the road against the Tennessee Titans (24-20). They pulled out both games by narrow margins, a trait that defines this team well: they do not always blow teams out, but they find a way to close out games.

It is no small detail to remember where they come from: Philadelphia lifted the Super Bowl by defeating the Kansas City Chiefs 40-22, after a devastating postseason that included a 55-23 win over Washington in the conference final. They are the defending champions, and they wear it well.

The Bears, meanwhile, come in with mixed emotions. They opened the season with an offensive showcase, an impressive 59-37 win at the home of the Carolina Panthers, only to then crash at Soldier Field: 3-9 against the Minnesota Vikings, a game in which the offense completely disappeared.

That contrast—from 59 points to barely 3 in one week—sums up Chicago's challenge: finding consistency. With a 1-1 record, this matchup against the champion is the perfect test to measure what they're made of.

Eagles vs Bears H2H: the pending rematch

The most recent precedent between these two teams carries weight, and a lot of it. In Week 13 of last season, the Bears visited Philadelphia and came away with a convincing 24-15 win, one of the Eagles' stumbles along the way.

Now the scenario is reversed: Chicago plays at home and Philadelphia will want to strike back. For the Bears, winning again would be a statement; for the Eagles, it is a score to settle.

Standings implications on the road to the Playoffs

The overall picture of the league shows the Eagles settled near the top: they lead the NFC East with a 2-0 record and sit in eighth place overall in the NFL. The Bears, at 1-1, are third in the NFC North—a division currently led by the Minnesota Vikings, precisely the team that shut them out offensively—and appear in ninth place in the overall landscape.

In a season start where there is still no room for slip-ups to pile up, this game carries mixed implications: a Chicago victory would put them squarely in the NFC conversation and hand the champion its first loss; a Philadelphia win would move them to 3-0 and strengthen their status as the team to beat in the conference.

The favorite according to the market and our pick to win Monday Night

The betting market has no doubts about who has the edge. The Eagles are listed as clear favorites on the moneyline, at 1.48 odds (66.5% implied probability), while the Bears are at 3.05 (33.5%).

In the point spread, Philadelphia is listed as the road team at -4.5 to -5.5, and the total points is set around 40.5 to 41.5, a relatively low number that suggests a tighter game rather than an open one.

The market and experience point to Philadelphia, and for good reason: they are the defending champion, come in undefeated, and have shown poise in close finishes. But the Bears already know what it is to beat this team, they will do it at home, and they have an offense capable of setting any scoreboard on fire when it shows up.

The forecast leans toward a narrow Eagles victory, in a low-scoring game that will likely be decided in the fourth quarter. If Chicago can sustain its offense throughout all four quarters and not the version Minnesota saw, the upset is far from impossible.

The betting market has no doubts about who has the edge. The Eagles are listed as clear favorites on the moneyline, at 1.48 odds (66.5% implied probability), while the Bears are at 3.05 (33.5%).

The forecast leans toward a narrow Eagles victory, in a low-scoring game that will likely be decided in the fourth quarter. If Chicago can sustain its offense throughout all four quarters and not the version Minnesota saw, the upset is far from impossible.

articles.standfirst: Jalen Hurts stayed down after a late hit from Chicago's D'Marco Jackson on Monday Night Football, and the NFL stepped in to have him evaluated for a concussion.
articles.summary: Jalen Hurts stayed down after a late hit from Chicago's D'Marco Jackson on Monday Night Football, and the NFL stepped in to have him evaluated for a concussion.
articles.body:
The NFL stepped in to make sure Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts was OK after taking a hard hit on Monday Night Football against the Chicago Bears .

Hurts stayed down on the turf after a late hit from Chicago's D'Marco Jackson midway through the second quarter. According to the MNF broadcast, he was sent to the medical tent after a call from the NFL's New York offices asking that he be evaluated for a possible concussion.

With the Eagles trailing 7-0 , backup Andy Dalton came in for him and threw an interception in the end zone on third-and-goal from the Bears' 2-yard line. It capped a 95-yard drive that had put Philadelphia at first-and-goal on the Chicago 1-yard line .

Shortly afterward, Hurts appeared on the sideline yelling at the medical staff after leaving the blue tent.

"Jalen Hurts is out of the tent and on the sideline," The Philadelphia Inquirer's Jeff McLane wrote on his official X account. "Looks like he's fine. But the damage was done. Andy Dalton tosses killer interception in the end zone."

"Eagles QB Jalen Hurts was evaluated for a concussion and cleared to return," ESPN's Adam Schefter wrote on his official X account.

articles.title: Was the NFL wrong to Keep Jalen Hurts put? He was furious and the backlash is growing
articles.standfirst: Jalen Hurts’ concussion scare sparks outrage as Nick Sirianni erupts and Skip Bayless blasts the NFL
articles.summary: Jalen Hurts’ concussion scare sparks outrage as Nick Sirianni erupts and Skip Bayless blasts the NFL
articles.body:
The Eagles found themselves in a difficult spot against the Bears in Week 3 after Jalen Hurts took a hit from D'Marco Jackson and was sent for a concussion evaluation. Backup Andy Dalton came in and threw a costly interception with Chicago already in front.

Hurts' situation drew a strong reaction from Skip Bayless , who didn't hold back.

I'm great with protecting players, forcing concussion checks, but come on, NFL, BE READY. Took way too long to completely clear Jalen Hurts and he was rightfully furious about it.

Chicago made Philadelphia pay. Veteran Case Keenum , the Bears' third-string quarterback, took advantage of a coverage breakdown and threw a 41-yard touchdown pass to former Lions receiver Khalif Raymond , a play that swung the game.

The Bears controlled the yardage for most of the night, while Keenum surprised the home crowd with a brilliant performance that felt like a throwback.

The hit on Hurts also sent Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni into a rage, and he fired off a three-word insult at Jackson right after the play.

Philadelphia kept fighting but was overpowered by Ben Johnson's Bears , who scored 17 second-half points to build a 27-7 lead with just over seven minutes to play.

The Eagles have dominated the NFC East for years, but the Bears are starting to look like one of the conference's new powers. Johnson's team sent a message to the rest of the NFL, and Bayless made his own point loud and clear, though for entirely different reasons.

articles.title: Eagles seek those responsible for humiliating defeat suffered at the hands of the Bears
articles.standfirst: Turnovers, defensive problems and one controversial Nick Sirianni decision changed everything
articles.summary: Turnovers, defensive problems and one controversial Nick Sirianni decision changed everything
articles.body:
There was no single moment that doomed the Philadelphia Eagles at Soldier Field. Their first loss of the season was built piece by piece, through turnovers, penalties, defensive breakdowns and a handful of decisions that made an already difficult night even worse.

Chicago entered Monday night without starting quarterback Caleb Williams , leaving 38-year-old Case Keenum to make his first NFL start since 2023. That should have presented Philadelphia with an obvious opportunity to dictate the game.

Instead, Keenum looked composed from the outset, completing 24 of 34 passes for 247 yards and two touchdowns as Chicago moved the ball with surprising ease. Philadelphia , meanwhile, repeatedly sabotaged itself with three turnovers and 10 penalties in a 27-7 defeat.

The Eagles weren't simply beaten by an inspired backup quarterback. They gave Chicago opportunities and failed to respond when the game began slipping away.

Defense gave Keenum far too much comfort

The warning signs appeared on Chicago’s opening touchdown drive, when safety Marcus Epps missed two tackles as the Bears marched 66 yards.

Epps had already been under scrutiny after a difficult Week 2 performance against Tennessee, and his role appeared increasingly uncertain as Michael Carter II rotated into the secondary.

The problems went beyond one player. Drew Mukuba and Jihaad Campbell also struggled, while Philadelphia’s pass rush failed to consistently disturb Keenum in the pocket.

That inevitably puts defensive coordinator Vic Fangio under scrutiny. Bears head coach Ben Johnson repeatedly created space across the middle of the field, allowing Keenum to find open targets without needing to make particularly difficult throws.

Chicago’s approach was efficient rather than spectacular, but Philadelphia never found a convincing answer.

Quinyon Mitchell was the notable exception. The All-Pro cornerback broke up a fourth-and-goal pass in the first half and later denied Chicago again on third down, producing one of the few consistently strong defensive performances of the night.

Sirianni’s late punt becomes defining decision

Philadelphia still had opportunities to make the final stages uncomfortable for Chicago, which made Nick Sirianni ’s fourth-quarter decision particularly difficult to understand.

Trailing by 13 points, the Eagles faced fourth-and-1 at the Bears ’ 49-yard line. Philadelphia initially attempted to draw Chicago offside, took a delay-of-game penalty and then punted.

It was an extraordinarily cautious choice for a team needing two scores and running out of possessions.

The offense had already squandered enough chances. Andy Dalton entered when Jalen Hurts was evaluated for a concussion and threw an interception on his only passing attempt, turning the ball over near the goal line.

Saquon Barkley was one of the few offensive players who consistently threatened Chicago, rushing 15 times for 82 yards. Several additional gains were erased by penalties, adding to the sense that Philadelphia repeatedly got in its own way.

DeVonta Smith also provided a rare highlight with a superb 30-yard contested reception that helped set up Philadelphia’s only touchdown before halftime.

Rookie Makai Lemon flashed his ability on a couple of receptions, although the Eagles’ insistence on using him on short horizontal throws continues to limit his impact.

Philadelphia entered the night as the more settled team facing a third-string quarterback. By the end, Keenum had been the calmer player, Chicago had been the sharper team and the Eagles had produced a defeat in which the blame was spread almost everywhere.

articles.title: Bears vs Eagles: The United States national anthem sounded different in the NFL, and the reaction was quick to come
articles.standfirst: Mariachi Herencia de México's performance before the game generated mixed reactions on social media during a special night for the Latino community in Chicago.
articles.summary: Mariachi Herencia de México's performance before the game generated mixed reactions on social media during a special night for the Latino community in Chicago.
articles.body:
The national anthem of the United States was played in an unusual way before Monday Night Football between the Philadelphia Eagles and the Chicago Bears.

The presentation was part of the activities organized by the Bears for Latino Heritage Month . The team took advantage of the game against Philadelphia to celebrate Latino culture during an event also linked to “Vamos Bears” , its initiative to strengthen ties with Spanish-speaking fans.

A mariachi to perform the United States national anthem

Mariachi Herencia de México , a group originally from Chicago , brought mariachi violins and trumpets to one of the most traditional rituals in American sports.

The presentation also had a historic character: it was the first time that a mariachi group performed the national anthem of the United States at Soldier Field.

The performance in Chicago also had a precedent just a few days earlier. Mariachi Monumental de México, a group formed in Chicago in 2009, performed “The Star-Spangled Banner” before the game between Green Bay Packers and Atlanta Falcons at Lambeau Field . The group, which has performed at various sports venues across the United States, described its participation as a special moment in its career.

The ceremony brought together 76,955 spectators. After the performance, the Falcons defeated the Packers 35-14 after coming back from an early 7-0 deficit and stringing together 27 consecutive points during the game.

The performance divided social media

The fans' reaction quickly reached social media. Some spectators questioned the choice of the mariachi and argued that it should have preserved an interpretation closer to the traditional versions usually heard before games. Others received the performance in a completely different way. Numerous messages appeared celebrating the rendition, its energy, and the decision to incorporate one of the most recognizable musical expressions of Mexican culture into an NFL night .

An honor to perform the Star-Spangled Banner through our mariachi tradition.

The debate was not related to a change in the anthem's lyrics, but rather to the way chosen to perform it. The performance thus ended up becoming one of the most talked-about issues in the lead-up to Eagles-Bears.

In addition to the performance of the anthem, the event included a halftime presentation dedicated to the history and influence of Latin music in Chicago.

The game ended with a 27-7 victory for the Chicago Bears over the Philadelphia Eagles . Chicago, which entered the game with Case Keenum as quarterback, relied on a defensive performance that forced three turnovers and held Philadelphia to seven points.

articles.title: Jason Kelce had a small live TV slip-up and Pat McAfee didn't let it slide
articles.standfirst: A single phrase during ESPN's broadcast was enough for Pat McAfee to interrupt Jason Kelce's analysis and put the moment under the spotlight.
articles.summary: A single phrase during ESPN's broadcast was enough for Pat McAfee to interrupt Jason Kelce's analysis and put the moment under the spotlight.
articles.body:
On Monday, September 28, Monday Night Football took over Soldier Field in Chicago for the matchup between the Philadelphia Eagles and the Chicago Bears . Scott Van Pelt, Pat McAfee and Jason Kelce were following the game from the set and, up to that point, the broadcast had been moving along normally. Then came halftime analysis.

The comment that changed the tone of the analysis

Philadelphia went into halftime trailing 10-7, so Kelce took the floor to break down what had happened in the first half . He talked about the opportunities the offense had created, how the ball was moving and Jalen Hurts' performance.

But in the middle of his analysis, something caught attention. When referring to the Eagles, Kelce started using "we" instead of talking about the team from an outside perspective .

Pat McAfee didn't let the "we" slide

The slip became even more obvious when Kelce said: "We played really well offensively." That was enough for Pat McAfee to jump in with a joke from the same set: "A lot of we talk out of Jason for Philly."

Kelce burst out laughing when he realized what he had said and quickly corrected himself on camera: "Sorry Bears fans! Did I say we?"

The moment lasted only a few seconds, but there was a pretty clear reason the word came out so naturally.

13 seasons with the Eagles

Kelce spent all 13 seasons of his NFL career with the Philadelphia Eagles after the franchise selected him in 2011 . During that time, he became one of the team's most recognizable figures and was part of the roster that won Super Bowl LII in 2018 against the New England Patriots.

At the end of the 2023 season, he announced the end of his playing career. He soon began his next chapter as an ESPN analyst and is now in his third season in front of the cameras .

Did Jason Kelce receive any punishment?

There was no fine or suspension over the comment. The "we" was simply a slip during the broadcast and, more than anything, a reminder of how difficult it can be to break a habit built over 13 years .

articles.title: Philadelphia Eagles set franchise record in the worst possible way in loss to LA Rams
articles.standfirst: Quarterback Jalen Hurts couldn't get anything going with a depleted offensive supporting cast.
articles.summary: Quarterback Jalen Hurts couldn't get anything going with a depleted offensive supporting cast.
articles.body:
It’s almost unfathomable that Jalen Hurts could finish an NFL game with only 93 passing yards . Hurts has won a Super Bowl with the Philadelphia Eagles and turned into one of the best, and sometimes most underrated, quarterbacks in the league.

But Hurts couldn’t get anything going against the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday. To be fair to Hurts, he was missing his three best offensive players. DeVonta Smith and Dallas Goedert couldn't play in this game due to injuries, and Saquon Barkley had to leave the game midway through it.

The multitude of injuries, along with Hurts and the rest of his weapons not meshing well with new offensive coordinator Sean Mannion just yet, resulted in a historically poor performance on Sunday.

Philadelphia Eagles didn't convert a single third down against the Rams

As mentioned during the broadcast of the game, and confirmed by stat-tracker QBgami , the Eagles had the worst third-down performance in the entire history of the franchise: they went 0-for-12 on third down attempts .

Philadelphia's defense was able to keep the team in it, despite having to take the field way too often, in a game full of tons of possessions. Ultimately, the defense began cracking late in the game, and the Eagles offense put up zero points in the second half.

With the Eagles facing second-and-8 and 14:15 remaining in the first quarter, Elijah Moore lined up in a position that would have covered tight end E.J. Jenkins and risked an illegal formation.

Hurts noticed it before the snap: “Get off the f**king ball,” he shouted. Moore appeared to look back toward Hurts , prompting the quarterback to add, “Come on!”

The receiver quickly adjusted, and Philadelphia avoided a penalty. The play gained only one yard, however, and the Eagles eventually punted.

The moment stood out because Hurts rarely shows that kind of emotion publicly. By the end of the afternoon, though, it made more sense.

Eagles offense never found rhythm

Philadelphia managed only 172 total yards and went 0-for-12 on third down in a game it still had a chance to win late.

Hurts finished 12-of-27 for 93 passing yards with two touchdowns, but he was sacked four times and completed only two passes after halftime.

The Eagles had an opportunity to take a three-score lead midway through the fourth quarter, but Hurts’ fourth-and-goal attempt to Darius Cooper from the two-yard line fell incomplete.

Los Angeles responded with a 98-yard touchdown drive and completed the comeback.

“Poor execution. I don’t think there’s any other way to put it,” Hurts said afterward. “I have to be better. I have to figure it out. However it looks, whatever that means.”

Philadelphia has now lost two straight after opening the season 2-0.

Answer is more work, not excuses

Despite the frustration caught on the broadcast, Hurts returned to his familiar tone after the loss.

“I’m not going to make excuses. I’m not going to make promises,” Hurts said. “I’m just going to double down on the work and lead the best way I can and continue to have the confidence that I have in this group to forge and figure it out.”

He also insisted the Eagles are still growing into what they want to become.

“This is a team that is building and finding its way,” Hurts said. “It’s obviously a work in progress.”

The quarterback added: “I have the utmost confidence in this team. I have the utmost confidence in this group.”

The hot-mic moment with Moore should not be overread as a sign of a fractured locker room. What it did reveal was how much Philadelphia’s repeated mistakes are beginning to wear on its quarterback.

The Eagles face Jacksonville next, and the bigger issue is not whether Hurts lost his temper for a few seconds. It's whether Philadelphia can finally clean up the execution problems that caused it.

articles.title: Jason Kelce makes terrible mistake on his NFL Network debut
articles.standfirst: The former Eagles center impressed in the booth before Dave Pasch had to correct him during Colts-Commanders in London
articles.summary: The former Eagles center impressed in the booth before Dave Pasch had to correct him during Colts-Commanders in London
articles.body:
Jason Kelce had barely put a foot wrong in his first game as an NFL analyst when years of muscle memory finally caught up with him.

Calling the Indianapolis Colts ’ win over the Washington Commanders in London alongside Dave Pasch and Kurt Warner , Kelce impressed with detailed analysis of blocking schemes, protection breakdowns and life in the trenches.

Then, while discussing Washington’s defense in the third quarter, he accidentally used the franchise’s former nickname. Pasch immediately jumped in.

“Commanders. You did it,” he said. Kelce initially had no idea what Pasch meant.

“What’d I do?” he asked before being told about the slip. Once it clicked, Kelce could only laugh at himself. “Oh my gosh! I almost made it out,” he said. “Sorry, Washington.”

Kelce already joked about making the mistake

The timing made the moment even better. Pasch revealed that before kickoff, he, Kelce and Warner had discussed the possibility that one of them might accidentally use Washington’s former name.

According to Pasch , the trio even had a “little gentlemen’s bet who would be first.” Kelce ended up being the one who lost it.

Washington retired its former nickname - The Redskins - in 2020 after years of criticism from Native American groups and other organizations. The franchise spent two seasons as the Washington Football Team before officially becoming the Commanders in 2022.

Kelce ’s mistake was understandable given the amount of time he spent playing against Washington . He anchored Philadelphia’s offensive line throughout a 13-year Eagles career, meaning the old name was part of his vocabulary for most of his time in the NFL.

Blunder did little to overshadow strong debut

Outside of that brief mistake, Kelce ’s first game in the booth was widely notable for how comfortable he sounded.

He repeatedly broke down what was happening at the line of scrimmage, explaining missed protections and pressure looks in a way that gave viewers more context without slowing the broadcast.

One particularly strong sequence came when Washington was forced to use another quarterback and Kelce explained how a new cadence can create problems for offensive linemen.

He then drew on his own experience with former Eagles backup Nate Sudfeld.

“I had a snap like a rocket… Fumble; everybody’s yelling at Nate Sudfeld. I’m like, ‘Dude, I am so sorry,’” Kelce recalled.

Kelce is scheduled to work three more NFL Network games this season, including Eagles-Jaguars in London on October 11.

That assignment may produce a different kind of challenge. Calling Washington by the right name is one thing. Staying completely neutral while his former team is on the field could be tougher.

articles.title: Lane Johnson retires from the NFL as one more Eagles season means time he can’t get back
articles.standfirst: The two-time Super Bowl champion steps away at 36, leaving Philadelphia with a major loss
articles.summary: The two-time Super Bowl champion steps away at 36, leaving Philadelphia with a major loss
articles.body:
Lane Johnson wanted one last season with his teammates. Three games into his 14th NFL campaign, the Philadelphia Eagles’ longtime right tackle decided his family and mental health needed him more. He announced his retirement on October 6, two days after missing Philadelphia’s game against the Los Angeles Rams for personal reasons.

“Right now, it is critical that I focus on my mental health,” Johnson wrote in his farewell statement. The 36-year-old explained that his priorities had changed and that he could no longer give football the complete commitment he believed his teammates, coaches and fans deserved.

Lane Johnson’s goodbye carries a message he spent years helping others hear

For Johnson, speaking openly about mental health has long been part of his life beyond football. In 2021, he stepped away from the Eagles while dealing with anxiety and depression, then publicly discussed his experience after returning. His willingness to explain what he was facing helped challenge the idea that an elite athlete’s strength makes him immune to emotional struggles.

He subsequently became an advocate for accessible support, partnering with Kooth to raise awareness of mental health resources for Philadelphia’s young people. The Eagles nominated him for the 2023 Walter Payton NFL Man of the Year Award. In their retirement tribute, owner Jeffrey Lurie praised that advocacy alongside his football achievements, saying Johnson’s courage in sharing his experiences had saved lives.

The football résumé is extraordinary: 171 regular-season games, all starts, six Pro Bowl selections and five Associated Press All-Pro honors, including two first-team selections. Johnson helped Philadelphia reach three Super Bowls and win two. He also blocked for two NFL rushing champions, LeSean McCoy and Saquon Barkley a reminder that some of his finest work appears beside somebody else’s name in the record book.

His route there was anything but obvious. Johnson began his college career as a 202-pound quarterback at Kilgore College before transferring to Oklahoma and eventually becoming an offensive tackle. Philadelphia selected him fourth overall in 2013. The former passer became a cornerstone of the protection and running lanes that powered the franchise’s most successful era.

There had already been a deeply personal explanation for why the end was approaching. In August, Johnson said 2026 would probably be his final season and spoke about his oldest child turning 13. “It’s hard to get time back,” he said. That observation now gives his retirement letter particular weight: another season was available, but those years with his children would not wait.

Philadelphia must now replace a cornerstone player amid a 2-2 start to the season. Johnson leaves with memories of two championship parades down Broad Street and a farewell that puts his children, family and well-being at the heart of his next chapter. After years helping others understand the importance of seeking mental health support, he is now following his own advice, making his family his sole priority. Wishing him all the best!

articles.title: Why were Jeremiah Trotter Jr. and Bryan Thomas Jr. ejected at the kickoff of the Eagles-Jaguars game in London?
articles.standfirst: The players were ejected following an altercation during the opening kickoff. Jacksonville's touchdown return was also called back due to a penalty.
articles.summary: The players were ejected following an altercation during the opening kickoff. Jacksonville's touchdown return was also called back due to a penalty.
articles.body:
The game between the Philadelphia Eagles and the Jacksonville Jaguars in London got off to an unusual start. Barely 13 seconds had passed when Jeremiah Trotter Jr. , a Philadelphia linebacker, and Bryan Thomas Jr ., a Jacksonville defensive player, were ejected after getting into a fight at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

It all started with the opening kickoff. Josh Cameron returned the ball to the end zone, but Jacksonville’s touchdown was nullified due to penalties. Amid the confusion, the two players clashed , and the referees ultimately ejected them.

Trotter Lost a Key Player for the Eagles

The ejection was a setback for the Eagles, who entered the game with several players out and needed to regain ground after two consecutive losses. Trotter had emerged as a key player on defense following his performance against the Los Angeles Rams , a game in which he recorded 15 tackles, ten of them solo. In the first four games of the season, he had racked up 19 tackles and one pass deflection.

In Jacksonville, the player ejected was Bryan Thomas Jr., defensive end No. 57, not Brian Thomas Jr., the No. 7 wide receiver and one of the Jaguars’ key offensive weapons.

A Family Precedent for Jeremiah Trotter Jr.

The incident had a striking family precedent. Jeremiah Trotter, father of the Eagles’ linebacker, was also ejected before a game in 2005, while playing for Philadelphia . On that occasion, the veteran linebacker was involved in an altercation during warm-ups before a game against the Atlanta Falcons.

The incident that just occurred added even more tension to a game that was important for both teams. Jacksonville arrived in London with a 3-1 record, while Philadelphia arrived with a 2-2 record and coming off two consecutive losses. The game is part of Week 5 and is the first of two consecutive games the Jaguars will play in the United Kingdom.

More than two decades later, his son was at the center of a similar scene, though this time the incident occurred after the kickoff and with the game already underway. In London, the first play ended without a touchdown and with two players on their way to the locker room before the offenses could even run their first play.

articles.title: Nick Sirianni is to blame for the Eagles' debacle against the Jaguars
articles.standfirst: Philadelphia led Jacksonville with eight seconds left, but managed to lose the game
articles.summary: Philadelphia led Jacksonville with eight seconds left, but managed to lose the game
articles.body:
N ick Sirianni has accepted responsibility for the Philadelphia Eagles ’ 19-17 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars in London, acknowledging that his late kickoff decision helped determine the outcome after his team appeared poised to escape with a victory.

Philadelphia led 17-16 with eight seconds remaining when Jake Elliott converted a 48-yard field goal but instead of sending the ensuing kickoff into the end zone, the Eagles opted for a shorter kick.

Giving Jacksonville one final opportunity to respond, Ameer Abdullah returned the ball 53 yards to the Eagles ’ 39-yard line, putting the Jaguars in position to attempt a decisive field goal kick.

Cam Little then connected from 57 yards as time expired at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium , completing a dramatic comeback in the most unlikely of fashions, leaving the Eagles ’ head coach with a bitter taste in his mouth.

“I didn’t make the right decision, and I lost us that game,” Sirianni confessed. “That’s what I said to our guys, and what hurts there is that, you know, the guys fought so hard and then I don’t make the decision that, you know, that I should make at the end of the game, and I cost us that game, and I put that fully on me.

"At the end of the day, I didn’t make the right decision, and it cost us the game. You know, and so there’s no other way around it. There’s nothing really else to say about that. It’s just I didn’t do my job good enough in that situation."

Eagles must respond after another costly loss in NFC East race

The defeat came after Philadelphia had surrendered its advantage late in the fourth quarter as Trevor Lawrence found Parker Washington for a 27-yard touchdown, leaving the Eagles needing Elliott ’s late field goal to regain the lead before Jacksonville ’s final possession.

The finish also echoed Dallas ’ recent loss to Baltimore as the Cowboys had sent a kickoff into the end zone, but the Ravens still got into field-goal range as Tyler Loop delivered the winner, so Philadelphia ’s different approach still produced a painful result.

But the problems extended beyond the final seconds as without leading rusher Saquon Barkley and receiver DeVonta Smith , the Eagles struggled offensively, finishing with just 22 rushing yards while dealing with difficulties along a makeshift offensive line.

Jalen Hurts completed 21 of 40 passes for 220 yards and a touchdown, connecting with Darius Cooper for a 62-yard score whilst Will Shipley added a two-yard rushing touchdown as Jacksonville , meanwhile, improved to 4-1.

Washington caught two touchdowns from Lawrence as the wide receiver recorded six receptions for 124 yards, helping the Jaguars recover after falling behind in the first half.

Philadelphia dropped to 2-3 and the Eagles must now address their offensive shortcomings, and their next opportunity comes against the Carolina Panthers at Lincoln Financial Field on Sunday, October 18 as they look to remain in the NFC East race.

articles.title: Eagles Legend Donovan McNabb steps up to defend Jalen Hurts
articles.standfirst: The Eagles suffered another heartbreaking loss, but Donovan McNabb believes Jalen Hurts is not to blame for Philadelphia’s collapse.
articles.summary: The Eagles suffered another heartbreaking loss, but Donovan McNabb believes Jalen Hurts is not to blame for Philadelphia’s collapse.
articles.body:
A new controversial defeat for the Philadelphia Eagles was confirmed this weekend in London. The loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars left plenty of unanswered questions, but franchise legend Donovan McNabb stepped up to defend Jalen Hurts , insisting that the quarterback did everything necessary to put his team in position to win.

The Eagles’ offense was far from perfect. Once again, the unit lost momentum in the second half and failed to capitalize on key opportunities.

However, when the game was on the line, Hurts delivered. With fewer than 10 seconds remaining on the clock, Philadelphia took the lead, and the quarterback left the field believing his team would close out the victory. Instead, the special teams failed to finish the job: Jacksonville returned the kickoff and secured the win with a game-winning field goal on the final play.

Donovan McNabb backs Jalen Hurts after loss to Jaguars

McNabb has never been one to hide his opinions when it comes to Eagles quarterbacks. This time, the former Philadelphia star praised Hurts’ performance and defended his execution in the final moments.

“It was a great drive orchestrated by our quarterback, Jalen. Jalen put us in position [to win],” McNabb said on 94WIP.

“I just think for our last drive, Jalen put us in position to win the game, hands down. No matter what else they want to nitpick with the eight seconds left on the clock, I’m just going to look at it from a former player’s perspective and now from an analyst standpoint: I did everything I needed to do for us to win the game. We kicked the field goal, we were up.”

Much of the criticism following the loss has been directed at Nick Sirianni, who admitted he could have made better decisions in the final moments. The choice to allow Jake Elliott to attempt a kick that could be returned was heavily questioned.

For McNabb, however, the issue was execution rather than the decision itself. The former quarterback believes Philadelphia needed to trust its special teams unit to finish the game.

“We allowed them to run it out, which was fine,” McNabb added. “We just have to cover. We didn’t cover. That was bad on our special teams.”

The Eagles fell 19-17 to Jacksonville in London and suffered their third consecutive loss , dropping their record to 2-3 on the season . Philadelphia will now look to bounce back next Sunday against the Carolina Panthers at home.

articles.title: Nick Sirianni is going through his worst moment with the Philadelphia Eagles, and legend Michael Vick is asking for him to be given more time
articles.standfirst: Philadelphia’s three-game losing streak has intensified calls for change, but former Eagles quarterback Michael Vick believes the franchise should remain patient
articles.summary: Philadelphia’s three-game losing streak has intensified calls for change, but former Eagles quarterback Michael Vick believes the franchise should remain patient
articles.body:
N ick Sirianni is facing one of the toughest stretches of his Philadelphia Eagles tenure, with a disappointing start to the 2026 NFL season putting his leadership under the microscope.

After three consecutive defeats, frustration is growing among fans, but franchise legend Michael Vick has delivered a clear message: the coach deserves more time.

Philadelphia has fallen to 2-3 after losing to the Chicago Bears , Los Angeles Rams and Jacksonville Jaguars .

The latest setback was particularly painful, as the Eagles appeared to have secured a victory in London before a late Jacksonville comeback turned a narrow lead into a 19-17 defeat.

The team's official record and upcoming schedule underline the urgency of the situation, with Carolina next before a major divisional clash against Dallas.

Vick , who starred for Philadelphia during his playing career, believes supporters should not overlook what Sirianni and quarterback Jalen Hurts have accomplished together.

Speaking about the growing criticism, he urged Eagles fans to show patience rather than immediately demanding a coaching change.

"It's just a couple more years, year to, it'll start a trend back in the right direction," Vick said.

"And then they got the right coach too, man. Everybody need to get off Nick's back, man. Sometimes I like to use my platform to say what I want to say. This is your platform. So right now I got the floor.

"I'm just saying, man, you got a good leader and a great coach and you got that tandem of head coach and quarterback. Leave it alone. I love, I ain't gonna disrespect our Eagles fans, but I'm always telling the truth because they real. But let this combination ride out, baby. Don't get too impatient right now. You know what I'm saying? Work yourself out."

articles.title: Terrell Owens criticizes Stephen A. Smith and doesn't understand why ESPN didn't suspend him for his comments about an NFL legend
articles.standfirst: The Pro Football Hall of Famer believes Smith's apology isn't enough and wants ESPN to hold its outspoken personality accountable
articles.summary: The Pro Football Hall of Famer believes Smith's apology isn't enough and wants ESPN to hold its outspoken personality accountable
articles.body:
Terrell Owens is demanding accountability from ESPN after Stephen A. Smith faced backlash for his remarks about Philadelphia Eagles offensive tackle Lane Johnson's decision to retire and prioritize his mental health.

The Pro Football Hall of Famer believes Smith's apology shouldn't be the end of the controversy and wants the network to consider disciplinary action.

Speaking on his Get TO the Point podcast, Owens questioned why the longtime sports commentator hadn't been suspended after discussing such a sensitive subject on national television.

Johnson announced his retirement on October 6, ending a 14-season career spent entirely with Philadelphia. The two-time Super Bowl champion explained that his priorities had changed, with his mental well-being and spending more time with his family becoming increasingly important.

The following day, Smith addressed Johnson's unexpected departure during ESPN's First Take. He questioned the timing of the decision and connected it to the Eagles' early-season struggles.

His remarks drew criticism, including from fellow ESPN personality Kimberley A. Martin , who challenged the way Johnson's situation was being discussed.

Smith subsequently apologized during the October 8 broadcast, acknowledging that his comments had made light of a serious mental health issue.

Owens questions ESPN's response to Smith's controversy

Owens isn't convinced that an apology is enough to resolve the situation. He believes ESPN should explain why Smith hasn't faced further consequences, especially given the network's influence and the reach of its most recognizable personalities.

“I don’t understand how there’s not any consequences to Stephen A.’s actions, especially with ESPN and Disney being the corporation, the business entity that they are, to speak so insensitive with a topic like mental health the way he did, why isn’t he suspended? Why?” said Owens .

“For him to speak so recklessly to a guy and then try to backtrack and say he’s had mental health issues, then if you knew that, then you’re smart enough to not speak on something affecting millions of people that’s a very sensitive topic.

“To feel like you have a microphone and a platform and be reckless with your words, he’s never played football. Maybe his mental is not the same as a football person’s mental.

“His stresses or whatever he’s going through up to leading where he is getting paid by ESPN, that mental doesn’t even compare to a football player’s mental and what we have to go through.”

Owens and Smith have had public disagreements in the past, adding another dimension to the criticism.

ESPN hasn't announced a suspension over Smith's remarks about Johnson . The absence of publicly announced disciplinary action has left questions about how the network feels about the incident and whether it considers the apology sufficient.
