articles.title: Concern over Jalen Hurts' blood clot: what medical experts say
articles.standfirst: Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts will miss Sunday's game against the Carolina Panthers
articles.summary: Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts will miss Sunday's game against the Carolina Panthers
articles.body:
Concern is growing over Jalen Hurts ' health after the Philadelphia Eagles confirmed that the quarterback would be unavailable for their Week 6 matchup.

The decision came after medical examinations showed that a small blood clot in his leg had moved, prompting the team to reassess his condition.

According to the Eagles , Hurts first sought treatment for calf discomfort on October 8 after being cleated during the October 4 game against the Los Angeles Rams .

An ultrasound performed in London before Philadelphia's game against the Jacksonville Jaguars detected a superficial blood clot. Team doctors initially determined that he could safely play, but a follow-up scan on October 14 revealed movement in the clot.

The Eagles subsequently ruled Hurts out against Carolina, stressing that his health and safety were the priority. The team has not announced a return date, as doctors determine the appropriate course of treatment.

Former NFL physician David Chao , known as Pro Football Doc, explained that the word superficial is an important distinction when assessing the situation.

However, he warned that such clots should not be dismissed simply because they are not initially classified as deep-vein thrombosis.

"It's still said to be superficial. Deep vein thrombosis are what is difficult and dangerous. Superficial can progress to deep Right now they're saying superficial. He's clearly missing this game. The Eagles are taking every precaution, but here's the issue."

Chao also raised questions about what caused the clot and whether medication might be necessary. He cautioned that blood thinners could complicate a return to football because of the potential consequences of bleeding following a collision.

Chao added that the cause of the clot must be understood before doctors can determine the best approach.

"What caused it? Was it inactivity on the flight and the cleating and accidental and superficial, or is there now potentially a deeper issue? Does he need to be anticoagulated? If he needs blood thinners, he will be ruled out because of the risk of bleed, especially a hit to the head brain bleed. You can’t have that."

What medical experts say about the risks

Dr. Dinesh Dhanaraj , an orthopedic surgeon who spoke to PhillyVoice, explained that superficial clots can develop after a blow to the leg and are generally less dangerous than deep-vein thrombosis.

However, movement or growth can raise concerns about the clot extending into deeper veins, potentially leading to a pulmonary embolism.

Dr. Alina Mitina , an emergency medicine physician at Hackensack University Medicine, also highlighted the importance of considering both injury and prolonged inactivity when assessing clot risk. The precise cause and treatment for Hurts' condition have not been publicly confirmed.

Medical guidance from the NHS and Mayo Clinic explains that treatment depends on the clot's location and severity. Some superficial clots can be managed with supportive care, while others may require blood-thinning medication and monitoring.

An ultrasound helps doctors assess the clot and distinguish superficial thrombosis from DVT.

Chao warned that recovery could take longer if further treatment is needed: “Until we figure out the cause of this, we won’t know the cure. But anytime a blood clot is involved, it easily could involve multiple weeks. Let’s hope it’s superficial, not deep. Let’s hope it’s not progressing. Let’s hope he doesn’t have to be on long-term anticoagulants, or it could have a huge impact.”

The Eagles have not provided a timetable for Hurts ' return. For now, the priority is establishing whether the clot is stabilising and determining the safest treatment plan.

The medical opinions discussed here are general assessments, not a diagnosis of Hurts' individual condition; only the doctors treating him can determine his prognosis.

articles.title: Kylie Kelce reveals his underwear preferences and offers advice to Mikaela Shiffrin: “It doesn't squeeze and keeps everything in place”
articles.standfirst: The mom of four explains why she avoids visible panty lines and shares her go-to underwear style
articles.summary: The mom of four explains why she avoids visible panty lines and shares her go-to underwear style
articles.body:
Kylie Kelce is opening up about her underwear preferences, explaining why she favors thongs and what she looks for when choosing a comfortable pair.

The podcast host recently discussed the subject with Olympic skiing champion Mikaela Shiffrin , sharing her thoughts on fit and finding underwear that works for her body.

During a segment called “Why Tho” on Shiffrin’s What’s the Point podcast, Kelce traced her preference back to her field hockey days. Because the sport frequently required her to squat, she became conscious of visible panty lines beneath her clothes.

Joking about her curvier figure at the time, she explained that she wanted a smooth appearance, primarily for her own comfort and confidence.

“I wanted it to be smooth,” said Kelce . “Not for anybody else but myself, and so I have carried that into my adult life. Here’s the deal. I’ll wear a granny panty. I just, I do prefer a thong.”

Although Kelce acknowledged that she’s happy to wear fuller-coverage underwear, she admitted that thongs remain her preferred choice. Shiffrin , meanwhile, revealed that she generally opts for granny panties, prompting a lighthearted discussion about their differing tastes.

Kylie Kelce shares her tips for finding comfortable underwear

Kelce revealed that she regularly wears just two thong brands, singling out a high-cut design she believes comes from Abercrombie. She appreciates its lightweight fabric and shape, which allows it to sit comfortably on her hips without digging into her sides.

The ideal pair for Kelce shouldn't pull, pinch or feel restrictive. Instead, it should rest naturally against the skin while keeping everything securely in place. She also explained that the design helps her avoid uncomfortable pressure around her hips, making it a practical choice for everyday wear.

Promising to double-check the brand, she offered to send Shiffrin the details so the Olympic champion could consider trying it herself.

The mother of four previously explained that she no longer expects to wear a string bikini, preferring the idea of a high-waisted design or a swimsuit offering more coverage. After welcoming four daughters with her husband, retired Philadelphia Eagles star Jason Kelce , she said she prioritises what feels comfortable for her body.

Beyond fashion and body image, Kelce has also spoken openly about managing the demands of family life. During an appearance on the IMO podcast with Michelle Obama and Craig Robinson , she credited her parents, who live nearby, with providing invaluable childcare support.

The couple also employs a nanny during regular working hours, allowing them to balance busy professional schedules while remaining closely involved in raising their children.

“Now, granted, we do have a nanny,” she said. “I always give a shout out because we couldn’t do it without her, but we have her during regular work hours and really nothing outside of that.”

articles.title: A doctor issues a serious warning about Jalen Hurts: "Don't be surprised when the next news is that his season is over"
articles.standfirst: The Eagles placed their quarterback on injured reserve with a superficial blood clot in his calf. The franchise has not yet set a timetable for his return, and the treatment will be decisive in determining how long he will be out.
articles.summary: The Eagles placed their quarterback on injured reserve with a superficial blood clot in his calf. The franchise has not yet set a timetable for his return, and the treatment will be decisive in determining how long he will be out.
articles.body:
Jalen Hurts' situation became even more complicated. The Philadelphia Eagles officially placed their quarterback on Injured Reserve (IR) due to the superficial blood clot detected in his calf, so he will have to miss at least the next four games.

The decision came after consulting with several doctors and specialists and leaves Hurts sidelined for an indefinite period. The move does not mean his season is over, but it does open the door to a much longer absence than initially expected.

Sports doctor Brian Sutterer warned that the situation could be more serious than expected. Although he is not part of the Eagles' medical team and has not examined Hurts, he pointed out that the next news could be that the quarterback will not play again this season.

Treatment will be key to knowing when he can return

Philadelphia has not yet announced what the definitive treatment will be. The franchise has stated that the clot is treatable and that the decision on when he will be able to play again will depend on the doctors overseeing his recovery.

One of the possibilities is the use of anticoagulant s. In cases that present certain risk factors, this treatment may be prolonged for around 45 days and would complicate Hurts' return because it is a contact sport, due to the risk of bleeding.

Hematologist Jordan Schaefer, of the University of Michigan, explained that this type of clot requires ongoing monitoring and that a single check-up is not necessarily enough.

"A lot of the time, what we do is follow people closely over time. It is not just a one-time visit and that's it", Schaefer explained . The specialist pointed out that doctors usually reassess how the patient is feeling and check whether signs such as swelling or redness have improved.

Schaefer also wanted to draw attention to an issue that can go unnoticed among athletes. "People often don't think about it in athletes and in those who don't have many other risk factors," he explained, before highlighting the importance of paying attention to symptoms both in athletes and in people who do not play sports.

The doctor added that the first symptoms—pain, swelling, redness, or sensations different from the usual—can easily be mistaken for a muscle injury. That is why he considers it important to detect these problems early: "We often want to catch these things fairly early. It can potentially get worse".

'Head coach Nick Sirianni also made the organization's stance clear: "Jalen's health is of the utmost importance to all of us".'

A clot that changed the landscape

The problem originated during the game against the Los Angeles Rams on October 4, when Hurts took a cleat to the calf. Four days later he went to the medical area to receive treatment for that injury for the first time.

On October 10, already in London to face the Jacksonville Jaguars, an ultrasound detected the superficial clot. Doctors then determined that he could play and considered that activity and mobility were important. Hurts played in the game and threw for 220 yards and a touchdown.

But a new ultrasound performed after the game showed movement in the clot . That finding led the Eagles to rule him out for the game against Carolina and, ultimately, to place him on injured reserve.

When could Jalen Hurts return?

His stay on IR forces Hurts to miss at least four games: Carolina Panthers, Dallas Cowboys, Washington Commanders and New York Giants. Philadelphia will then have its bye week and the franchise will be able to reevaluate the quarterback's situation.

The franchise has not set a timetable, and his return will depend on the progression of the clot and the treatment chosen.

The setback also comes at a difficult time for Philadelphia. The Eagles began the season with a 2-3 record and are in the midst of a three-game losing streak. Hurts had thrown for 933 yards, eight touchdowns, and three interceptions in his five games.

Tanner McKee takes command of the Eagles

With Hurts out, Tanner McKee will be the one in charge of leading Philadelphia's offense. The quarterback will take over as the starter against Carolina while the Eagles look to keep their offense competitive during the absence of their main star.

For now, the only certainty is that Hurts will be out for at least four games. The possibility that he may not play again this season exists as a scenario raised from outside the organization, but the Eagles have not announced that his season is over.

The evolution of the clot and the response to treatment will determine whether Hurts can return during the season or whether his absence ends up being much longer.

The problem originated during the game against the Los Angeles Rams on October 4, when Hurts took a cleat to the calf. Four days later he went to the medical area to receive treatment for that injury for the first time.

But a new ultrasound performed after the game showed movement in the clot . That finding led the Eagles to rule him out for the game against Carolina and, ultimately, to place him on injured reserve.
When could Jalen Hurts return?

His stay on IR forces Hurts to miss at least four games: Carolina Panthers, Dallas Cowboys, Washington Commanders and New York Giants. Philadelphia will then have its bye week and the franchise will be able to reevaluate the quarterback's situation.
The franchise has not set a timetable, and his return will depend on the progression of the clot and the treatment chosen.

The setback also comes at a difficult time for Philadelphia. The Eagles began the season with a 2-3 record and are in the midst of a three-game losing streak. Hurts had thrown for 933 yards, eight touchdowns, and three interceptions in his five games.

With Hurts out, Tanner McKee will be the one in charge of leading Philadelphia's offense. The quarterback will take over as the starter against Carolina while the Eagles look to keep their offense competitive during the absence of their main star.

For now, the only certainty is that Hurts will be out for at least four games. The possibility that he may not play again this season exists as a scenario raised from outside the organization, but the Eagles have not announced that his season is over.
The evolution of the clot and the response to treatment will determine whether Hurts can return during the season or whether his absence ends up being much longer.

The Philadelphia Eagles have been plunged into complete uncertainty following the devastating announcement that franchise quarterback Jalen Hurts has suffered a season-ending injury , specifically diagnosed with deep vein thrombosis.

This medical setback arrives at the absolute worst possible moment for Philadelphia, as the team finds itself mired in a grim four-game losing streak , the first four-game slide of head coach Nick Sirianni's tenure in the City of Brotherly Love.

The recent downward spiral was capped off by a frustrating 25-14 loss to the Carolina Panthers , dropping the squad to a disappointing 2-4 record on the season. To make matters worse, the offense must now rely on completely unproven leadership under center.

The coaching staff faces a daunting choice between Tanner McKee , who earned his first meaningful NFL start this week, and newly acquired quarterback Joe Milton , who was signed just last week. With zero combined NFL wins between the two backup options, Philadelphia’s offensive game plan is forced to undergo an emergency overhaul mid-season

This unexpected medical issue threatens to completely derail an era defined by historic high-level play in the NFC East.

Since Jalen Hurts officially took over as the full-time starting quarterback five seasons ago, Philadelphia established undeniable divisional dominance by capturing three division titles , including back-to-back crowns, a remarkable feat that no NFC East franchise had accomplished in over two decades.

Without their Pro Bowl signal-caller guiding the huddle, the organization now faces its darkest competitive moment in years as they struggle to save their 2026 NFL season from total collapse.

Yet, despite the nightmare situation, Philadelphia's postseason hopes are not entirely extinct; rival division contenders such as the Dallas Cowboys , Washington Commanders , and New York Giants have all stumbled out of the gate while struggling to accumulate victories in a chaotic, wide-open race.

The next three weeks will ultimately define Philadelphia's fate, as the team prepares to navigate three consecutive high-stakes divisional matchups.

How the offense adapts during this crucial stretch without Hurts will dictate whether the front office decides to stick with its current developmental options or aggressively pivot before the upcoming trade deadline.

Given the glaring inexperience between McKee and Milton , team executives may actively explore the trade market for a seasoned veteran capable of salvaging the offense.

articles.title: Jalen Hurts season-ending injury puts eagles medical staff under fire over alleged negligence
articles.standfirst: Doctors told Hurts not to sleep, but after more than 30 hours awake, they let him play in London
articles.summary: Doctors told Hurts not to sleep, but after more than 30 hours awake, they let him play in London
articles.body:
Days after placing Jalen Hurts on the injured reserve list, the Philadelphia Eagles officially confirmed today that the 2024 Super Bowl MVP will miss the remainder of the 2026 NFL season after developing blood clots in both of his lungs .

Hurts was originally diagnosed with a left calf superficial vein thrombosis on October 10 in London ahead of Philadelphia's matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars. Despite the diagnosis, Hurts started that game, a dramatic late-second loss, and subsequently underwent an ultrasound on Wednesday that revealed movement in the clot .

The franchise signal-caller missed Sunday’s 25-14 loss to the Carolina Panthers , marking the first four-game losing streak of the Nick Sirianni era . With Hurts sidelined indefinitely, third-year backup Tanner McKee assumes starting quarterback duties, flanked by Joe Milton and Cole Payton as depth options on the roster.

Medical Negligence Allegations Mount After Unbelievable 36-Hour Awake Detail

Moments after the season-ending news broke, NFL insider Tom Pelissero reported that following his initial diagnosis in London, medical staff instructed Hurts not to sleep as a precaution , resulting in the quarterback remaining awake for roughly 36 consecutive hours prior to throwing for 220 yards and a touchdown against Jacksonville.

The decision triggered immediate backlash across the medical community, with sports medicine analyst Dr. Jesse Morse labeling the situation a catastrophic failure and potential liability case for Philadelphia's staff, warning that pulmonary embolisms paired with career-related trauma could pose a threat to his playing career.

Morse detailed that a combination of frequent air travel, severe physical contact, and systemic risk factors make returning to a collision sport extraordinarily complex, asserting that clearing him under those circumstances represented immense negligence and predicting that independent specialists may hesitate to clear him for contact football anytime soon.

Uncertain Future Surrounds Jalen Hurts Contract Ahead of Pivotal Offseason

For now, the 28-year-old dual-threat quarterback will focus on recovery while undergoing evaluations from both team physicians and independent specialists, seeking clarity on a career that had previously been remarkably durable, having logged at least 15 games played in each of his first six professional seasons.

Hurts entered the 2026 campaign without securing an offseason extension, leaving his long-term financial security in Philadelphia somewhat fluid.

While team owner Jeffrey Lurie and general manager Howie Roseman have repeatedly voiced firm confidence in Hurts as the franchise centerpiece, his five-year, $255 million contract features critical financial benchmarks this coming spring, turning his recovery timeline and roster status into one of the most compelling storylines heading into the offseason.

articles.standfirst: Philadelphia coach defended the team's medical staff but offered few details about Hurts' clearance to play and travel
articles.summary: Philadelphia coach defended the team's medical staff but offered few details about Hurts' clearance to play and travel
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles have more immediate concerns than their disappointing 2-4 record, with questions surrounding Jalen Hurts ' medical treatment becoming an increasingly uncomfortable issue for head coach Nick Sirianni .

Hurts is expected to miss the remainder of the 2026 NFL season after being diagnosed with deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli, serious blood-clotting conditions that require treatment with blood thinners.

The diagnosis has prompted scrutiny of Philadelphia's decision to allow its starting quarterback to face the Jacksonville Jaguars in London despite doctors reportedly identifying a superficial blood clot beforehand.

Speaking Monday following the Eagles ' 25-14 defeat to the Carolina Panthers , Sirianni repeatedly referred questions about the decision to medical professionals rather than offering a detailed explanation.

The controversy centers on the circumstances preceding Philadelphia's Week 5 matchup against Jacksonville.

Hurts reportedly suffered an injury when he was cleated during the Eagles ' October 4 game against the Los Angeles Rams , before seeking medical treatment several days later.

An ultrasound in London reportedly identified a superficial clot, but the quarterback received clearance to play against the Jaguars .

According to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport, Hurts remained in hospital until approximately 4 a.m. before the game.

Asked why the Eagles considered it safe for Hurts to participate, Sirianni emphasized the organization's commitment to player welfare.

"The health of our players is always at the forefront of our mind," Sirianni told reporters. "Leave that up to the medical experts. We always, always care deeply about our players."

Eagles coach refuses to explain Hurts decision

The questioning intensified when reporters asked why Hurts had been permitted to take the team flight back to Philadelphia after playing against Jacksonville.

"Again, I'm not a medical expert," Sirianni responded. "We get medical information from our guys, and we always put the players health first and foremost in every situation."

Sirianni also expressed "full trust and full faith" in Philadelphia's medical staff when asked whether the situation should have been handled differently.

However, he declined to identify the medical personnel involved in discussions about Hurts ' availability or provide further details about the decision-making process.

Those unanswered questions have become particularly significant because deep vein thrombosis can lead to pulmonary embolism.

Hurts faces uncertain recovery

The Eagles and Hurts ' agent, Nicole Lynn , confirmed that the quarterback is clinically stable and receiving treatment for blood clots affecting both lungs.

Doctors expect a full recovery, but Hurts cannot participate in contact football while taking blood thinners.

Sports medicine specialist Dr. Brian Sutterer had previously warned that an initially superficial clot could develop into a more serious condition.

Philadelphia must now attempt to recover from four consecutive defeats without its starting quarterback, who recorded 933 passing yards and eight touchdowns before being sidelined.

Tanner McKee is expected to continue leading the offense when the Eagles face the Dallas Cowboys on October 26.

Although Sirianni maintains confidence in the medical staff, the organization has yet to provide a detailed public explanation of the decisions surrounding Hurts ' participation and subsequent travel.

With the quarterback's season potentially over, those questions are unlikely to disappear.

articles.summary: The Philadelphia Eagles quarterback has been ruled out for the rest of the season after doctors found multiple blood clots in his lungs.
articles.body:
It's a scary time for the Hurts family. Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts has been ruled out for the rest of the NFL season due to multiple blood clots in his lungs. This comes after Hurts played a game on October 11 despite dealing with a blood clot in his calf .

Hurts was told not to sleep, as a precaution, ahead of the game . Yet the medical team allowed him to play the game anyway. After further testing, it was revealed that Hurts is dealing with deep vein thrombosis and a bilateral pulmonary emboli - blood clots in his lungs .

The terrifying situation has the Eagles in the limelight. In just about everyone's eyes, Hurts should not have been allowed to play after the initial blood clot in his calf was discovered . Regardless, Hurts is stable and will now be treated, thankfully before it got any worse.

Pamela Hurts, Jalen Hurts' mom, says "things could always be worse"

While no one in Hurts' family, and even himself, have come out to speak about the situation, Jalen's mother Pamela Hurts did post a subliminal message on her TikTok account. She captioned the post, " Things could always be worse..... #gratitudeisasuperpower ". While walking around, she spoke about being grateful more than anything.

" Just a reminder y’all, be grateful. Be grateful for where you are and what you have because your life could change at a blink of an eye. Be grateful. What are you grateful for? "

The Hurts family is attacking this unfortunate news with positivity and optimism. Jalen should be able to recover and play next season, if everything goes as planned.

articles.title: NFL Network analyst apologizes for comments about Jalen Hurts after calls for his firing
articles.standfirst: Michael Robinson faces backlash after questioning the severity of Jalen Hurts' blood clot diagnosis
articles.summary: Michael Robinson faces backlash after questioning the severity of Jalen Hurts' blood clot diagnosis
articles.body:
NFL Network analyst Michael Robinson has apologized to Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts after facing widespread criticism for comments questioning the seriousness of his injury and raising doubts about his commitment to the team.

Robinson sparked controversy during an appearance on NFL GameDay Kickoff last Thursday while discussing Hurts ' initial diagnosis of a superficial blood clot in his calf.

“I don’t know nothing, guys, but it looked like they were trying to pin the outcome of this season on Jalen Hurts, just so that they can have an excuse later on to move on from Jalen Hurts,” said Robinson .

“And again, I’m not saying I know nothing, guys, but … if I’m Jalen Hurts or anybody in Jalen Hurts’ camp, I’m saying, ‘Well, if everybody’s hurt, I’m hurt, too.’

“Guys, I’ve been cleated before. And I’m not saying a superficial blood clot isn’t serious. I’m not saying that, but I would advise all of our viewers to Google ‘superficial blood clot’ as opposed to a real blood clot. And again, I’m not a medical guy.”

His remarks quickly attracted backlash on social media, with several fans demanding that NFL Network fire him. Others argued that Robinson owed Hurts a public apology for making assumptions about his health without having the medical expertise to assess his condition.

On Thursday, Robinson addressed the controversy, admitting his comments were unfounded and that he shouldn't have speculated about a player's medical situation or dedication to his team.

"I want to sincerely apologize to Jalen Hurts, his family, the Philadelphia Eagles organization and fan base for my comments last Thursday," wrote Robinson.

“They were unfounded and I never should’ve speculated on a health issue of a player nor his commitment to his team.”

Jalen Hurts' diagnosis raises serious concerns

The controversy intensified after further medical examinations revealed that Hurts had deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli, meaning blood clots had travelled to both lungs.

According to a statement released by the Eagles and Hurts ' agent, Nicole Lynn , the quarterback is clinically stable and has no significant functional limitations. However, he's receiving treatment with blood-thinning medication, which prevents him from participating in football activities involving contact.

Doctors reportedly expect Hurts to miss the remainder of the season, although his prognosis is positive and a full recovery is anticipated. The statement added that he could return to contact football once he no longer needs the medication, with no long-term effects expected.

Hurts initially suffered a calf injury after being struck by a cleat during Philadelphia's October 4 game against the Los Angeles Rams. An ultrasound conducted in London subsequently identified a superficial blood clot before the Eagles faced the Jacksonville Jaguars on October 11.

Despite the diagnosis, Hurts played against Jacksonville, attempting 40 passes in a narrow 19-17 defeat. Reports later revealed that he had spent much of the night undergoing medical evaluation before travelling to the stadium.

Lynn subsequently clarified that Hurts had managed to sleep before rejoining his teammates, following concerns about his condition and readiness to play.

The circumstances surrounding his participation have prompted questions about the Eagles' medical decision-making. Head coach Nick Sirianni defended the organization, insisting that player welfare remains a priority and expressing full confidence in the medical staff.

Philadelphia has struggled without its starting quarterback. Backup Tanner McKee started against Carolina on Sunday, completing 26 of 45 passes for 215 yards and one touchdown in a 25-14 defeat.

articles.title: Jason Kelce rejects opportunity to coach the Eagles: Reason behind his refusal
articles.standfirst: Philadelphia's protection problems have raised questions about the coaching staff
articles.summary: Philadelphia's protection problems have raised questions about the coaching staff
articles.body:
The solution to the Philadelphia Eagles ' offensive line problems might appear obvious to supporters who spent more than a decade watching Jason Kelce dominate in the trenches. However, the franchise legend believes returning to Philadelphia as a coach would be the wrong decision.

The Eagles have struggled to establish consistency along their offensive line this season, with injuries to three starters during the opening weeks placing additional pressure on quarterback Jalen Hurts and the running game.

Those difficulties have intensified scrutiny of new offensive line coach Chris Kuper , who inherited the position after Jeff Stoutland departed following 13 seasons with the organization.

Kelce has continued visiting the team since retiring in 2024, but when asked whether he could take on a more significant coaching role, the former center explained why that possibility remains unlikely.

Speaking on SportsRadio 94WIP, Kelce revealed that he had spent time with Philadelphia's offensive linemen during training camp, learning the system and offering guidance.

"I was there in training camp a little bit and learning the offense a little bit and trying to help those guys," Kelce said.

He acknowledged that former players can provide useful insight, particularly when they have spent years performing the same responsibilities at the highest level.

However, Kelce was reluctant to suggest that his decorated playing career automatically qualified him to become an NFL coach.

"I think that there's probably people that are far more experienced and knowledgeable than I am," he admitted.

His explanation ultimately centered on two issues, those being a demanding personal schedule, and the availability of experienced offensive line coaches better equipped for the position.

"The reality is one, I don't have the time to do that," Kelce said.

He emphasized that he would continue offering occasional assistance, but could not commit the hours necessary to make a meaningful contribution every week.

Stoutland influence shapes Kelce's view

Kelce understands the importance of specialist coaching after spending much of his career working under Stoutland, who helped develop one of the NFL's most respected offensive lines.

During his retirement speech, Kelce delivered an emotional tribute to his former coach.

"No one has been more influential or meaningful to my success on the field in my career than Stout," he said.

That experience helped Kelce appreciate the preparation, teaching and personal investment required to coach professional players.

Although he has previously expressed interest in coaching high-school football, Kelce has consistently acknowledged that NFL responsibilities would demand more time than he is prepared to sacrifice.

Family and ESPN career remain priorities

Since leaving the Eagles , Kelce has built a prominent media career, joining ESPN's Monday Night Countdown and continuing his successful New Heights podcast with brother Travis Kelce .

He also shares four daughters with his wife, Kylie Kelce , and has repeatedly emphasized the importance of spending time with his family.

"I would love to coach," Kelce previously said. "The problem with coaching is the time, huge time commitment."

Kelce 's decision doesn't mean he has distanced himself from Philadelphia. His willingness to visit practices and advise players demonstrates that his connection to the organization remains strong.

However, the responsibility for fixing the Eagles ' offensive line ultimately rests with Kuper and the current coaching staff, rather than a franchise legend enjoying life after football.

"The reality is one, I don't have the time to do that," Kelce said.

Kelce understands the importance of specialist coaching after spending much of his career working under Stoutland, who helped develop one of the NFL's most respected offensive lines.

Although he has previously expressed interest in coaching high-school football, Kelce has consistently acknowledged that NFL responsibilities would demand more time than he is prepared to sacrifice.

articles.title: Saquon Barkley sends powerful message on Jalen Hurts’ season-ending blood clots
articles.standfirst: Saquon Barkley believes Jalen Hurts will come back stronger after his season-ending blood clot diagnosis.
articles.summary: Saquon Barkley believes Jalen Hurts will come back stronger after his season-ending blood clot diagnosis.
articles.body:
S aquon Barkley broke his silence on Jalen Hurts ' health scare, sending a heartfelt message of support after it was confirmed that the Eagles quarterback will miss the rest of the season due to blood clots. Amid a difficult 2026 campaign for the Philadelphia Eagles , Barkley expressed full confidence that his teammate will come back stronger.

Barkley, now in his third season with Philadelphia after entering the NFL in 2018, has established himself as one of the league's premier running backs and played a pivotal role in the Eagles' Super Bowl LIX championship.

However, the star running back has not matched the production of his outstanding 2024 season. Injuries have also limited him this year, forcing him to miss multiple games and adding to Philadelphia's offensive struggles.

Things became even more challenging when Hurts was diagnosed with blood clots that spread from his calf to his lungs, a condition that ended his season prematurely.

Despite the devastating news, Barkley struck an optimistic tone while speaking to reporters on Thursday, expressing unwavering faith in Hurts' ability to overcome the setback

"Knowing Jalen, this is just a little setback. He’s going to come back better from it. It’s probably hard to see that right now, but I know the type of person Jalen is and I truly believe in that," Barkley said.

The Eagles face a defining stretch

Hurts' absence leaves the Eagles facing one of their biggest challenges in recent years. Without their franchise quarterback, Philadelphia must quickly find a way to stay competitive if it hopes to keep its playoff aspirations alive.

The Eagles enter this stretch of the season with a 2-4 record , sitting second in the NFC East , ahead of the Dallas Cowboys and Washington Commanders , but trailing the New York Giants .

In the overall NFC standings , Philadelphia sits 11th , ahead of Dallas and the Arizona Cardinals , but behind teams such as the New Orleans Saints and Atlanta Falcons .

The Eagles will look to get their season back on track when they host the Cowboys in Week 7 on Monday Night Football . Kickoff is set for 8:15 p.m. ET , and the rivalry matchup could prove pivotal in determining whether Philadelphia can keep its postseason hopes alive without Hurts.

articles.title: Eagles under fire: NFL investigates team medical staff over treatment of Jalen Hurts’ blood clot
articles.standfirst: Philadelphia faces questions over medical decisions after Hurts was diagnosed with blood clots in his lungs
articles.summary: Philadelphia faces questions over medical decisions after Hurts was diagnosed with blood clots in his lungs
articles.body:
The NFL and the NFL Players Association (NFLPA) are jointly reviewing how the Philadelphia Eagles handled quarterback Jalen Hurts’ blood clot diagnosis, following concerns about the medical decisions that allowed him to play in London earlier this month.

The announcement came on Sunday after the players’ union called for a full investigation into the care Hurts received before and during the team’s trip to face the Jacksonville Jaguars.

In a brief joint statement, the league and union confirmed they were “working together to review the matter.”

The case has attracted attention because Hurts was initially diagnosed with a superficial blood clot in his left calf but was cleared to play against Jacksonville on October 11. The Eagles said the issue followed a blow to his calf during their October 4 game against the Los Angeles Rams.

According to the team’s account, Hurts sought treatment after practice on October 8. He practiced the following day before travelling with the squad to London.

An ultrasound conducted after the team arrived detected a superficial clot, and medical staff, alongside doctors in London, concluded he could safely play. A follow-up examination was recommended after the game.

Hurts completed 21 of 40 passes for 220 yards and a touchdown against Jacksonville, but further testing after his return to Philadelphia revealed that the clot had progressed. He was ruled out against the Carolina Panthers and subsequently placed on injured reserve.

Questions mount over Hurts’ medical clearance

The Eagles and Hurts ’ agent, Nicole Lynn , later confirmed that he had developed deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli, meaning clots had reached both lungs.

His treatment includes blood thinners, which prevent him from taking part in football activities while he remains on the medication. The team and his representatives expect a full recovery and say they don't anticipate long-term effects.

The NFLPA had pressed for an investigation, saying that the facts needed to be established before anyone drew conclusions about the decisions made. The union argued that a thorough review was essential to ensuring players receive appropriate medical care and protection.

League officials have defended the process so far. NFL chief medical officer Dr Allen Sills described the Eagles’ approach as conservative and focused on the player, while Commissioner Roger Goodell said the league welcomed a review and maintained that protocols had been followed.

The NFL has also said its medical officials were in contact with the team and doctors in London.

The investigation will examine the timeline of Hurts ’ diagnosis, the medical assessments and the decision to clear him for the Jaguars game. No findings have been announced, and the review has yet to establish whether any errors occurred.

Hurts ’ absence is a major sporting setback for Philadelphia, but his recovery remains the immediate priority. The review could also have broader implications for how teams assess and manage potentially serious medical conditions moving forward.

articles.title: Bombshell Report: NFL 'furious' with Eagles over Jalen Hurts blood clot controversy
articles.standfirst: A joint review with the NFLPA has intensified scrutiny of Philadelphia's handling of the quarterback's serious medical condition
articles.summary: A joint review with the NFLPA has intensified scrutiny of Philadelphia's handling of the quarterback's serious medical condition
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles were already confronting a difficult season without their starting quarterback. Now, the controversy surrounding Jalen Hurts ' blood clot diagnosis has developed into a dispute that reportedly has NFL commissioner Roger Goodell and league officials deeply frustrated.

Philadelphia's decision to play Hurts after doctors identified a superficial blood clot has attracted considerable scrutiny, particularly following the subsequent discovery of more serious complications that could keep the quarterback sidelined for the remainder of the season.

However, according to the Philadelphia Inquirer, the NFL's frustration is not primarily directed at the medical decisions themselves. Instead, league officials are reportedly unhappy with the Eagles ' failure to provide clear public explanations about Hurts' examinations, treatment and travel arrangements.

The situation escalated Sunday when the NFL and NFL Players Association confirmed they were jointly reviewing the matter.

"The NFL and NFL Players Association are working together to review the matter," the organizations announced.

The Philadelphia Inquirer reported that several NFL sources expressed frustration with how the Eagles communicated Hurts' deteriorating condition, particularly after Goodell faced questions about the situation during last week's owners meetings in New York.

"They're furious," one longtime source with connections to the league office told the newspaper.

Hurts ' medical problems began when a bruise appeared on October 8. Doctors identified a stable superficial blood clot two days later, before the quarterback played on October 11.

Subsequent examinations revealed that the clot had moved, prompting Philadelphia to place Hurts on injured reserve on October 17.

Two days later, doctors diagnosed deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary emboli, serious complications that require extended treatment and could end his season.

The Eagles have provided limited public information about those developments, leaving head coach Nick Sirianni to address questions normally directed toward medical personnel.

NFL medical officer defends Hurts treatment decisions

Despite the criticism surrounding Philadelphia's communication, NFL chief medical officer Dr. Allen Sills has publicly supported the care Hurts received.

"The notion that there are external factors or that any of our physicians would put a player in harm's way, that's nonsense," Sills said.

He continued: "I think there was incredible vigilance, there was conservative care, state-of-the-art imaging that was done in London."

Sills also expressed confidence in the timing of the medical decisions, saying he believed everyone involved had acted with appropriate caution.

The NFLPA retains the option of pursuing a fully independent investigation if it believes the joint review has been obstructed or misled.

Eagles face growing scrutiny

The controversy adds another complication to Philadelphia's disappointing start, with the team sitting at 2-4 following four consecutive defeats.

Backup quarterback Tanner McKee is expected to lead the offense against the Dallas Cowboys on Monday Night Football while Hurts remains unavailable.

Meanwhile, general manager Howie Roseman and the Eagles ' senior medical personnel haven't publicly addressed the outstanding questions about the quarterback's treatment.

The reported anger within the NFL highlights the distinction between confidence in medical care and dissatisfaction with how sensitive information has been communicated.

With the joint review underway, Philadelphia faces continuing questions about its handling of a situation that has extended well beyond the football field.

articles.title: Blockbuster Proposal: How Broncos can land Eagles RB Saquon Barkley before trade deadline
articles.standfirst: A proposed three-piece package could tempt Philadelphia to consider moving its star running back
articles.summary: A proposed three-piece package could tempt Philadelphia to consider moving its star running back
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles are approaching a critical stretch of their season, and the possibility of moving Saquon Barkley has emerged as an unexpected talking point amid their struggles.

A 2-4 record, four consecutive defeats and the prolonged absence of quarterback Jalen Hurts have left Philadelphia facing difficult questions about its ability to compete this season.

Barkley remains one of the franchise's most important offensive players, but a proposed trade involving the Denver Broncos would give general manager Howie Roseman an opportunity to secure future draft capital while maintaining an experienced presence in the backfield.

Under the hypothetical agreement, Denver would receive Barkley in exchange for J.K. Dobbins , a 2027 second-round selection and a 2027 fifth-round pick.

Neither organization has been reported to have entered negotiations, although the proposal presents an interesting question about how aggressively both teams should approach the November 10 trade deadline.

The Broncos have opened the season 5-2 under head coach Sean Payton , strengthening their position in the AFC following Sunday's 30-16 victory over the Arizona Cardinals .

Quarterback Bo Nix delivered an impressive performance, throwing for 222 yards and a touchdown while adding a spectacular 62-yard rushing score.

Denver's offense has demonstrated explosive potential, but establishing a more consistent running game could make life easier for its young quarterback.

Barkley would provide a proven solution. The former NFL Offensive Player of the Year rushed for more than 2,000 yards during his first season with Philadelphia in 2024, establishing himself as one of the league's most dangerous offensive players.

His experience as both a runner and receiver would give Payton additional options, particularly against defenses attempting to pressure Nix.

However, Denver already has promising young backs in RJ Harvey and Jonah Coleman , making the sacrifice of two draft selections a significant consideration.

Eagles face difficult financial decision over Barkley

Philadelphia's willingness to consider a trade would depend heavily on the financial implications.

Barkley signed a two-year, $41.2 million contract extension in March 2025, with commitments extending through the 2028 season.

Moving him could accelerate salary-cap charges associated with previously paid bonuses, while Denver would need to accommodate his substantial future compensation.

Dobbins would provide Philadelphia with an experienced replacement, although he cannot be expected to reproduce Barkley 's individual impact immediately.

The draft compensation would offer Roseman additional opportunities to reshape the roster, particularly if the Eagles eventually decide their disappointing campaign requires more substantial changes.

Barkley's return could change Eagles' trade outlook

Philadelphia may soon receive a reminder of why Barkley remains so valuable.

The running back is reportedly trending toward returning against the Dallas Cowboys on Monday Night Football after missing two games with a hamstring injury.

Despite recording only 182 rushing yards across four appearances this season, Barkley has averaged 5.1 yards per carry while injuries have restricted his opportunities.

With Hurts sidelined and DeVonta Smith also unavailable, the Eagles need their most established offensive playmakers more than ever.

A productive return against Dallas could strengthen Philadelphia's hopes of recovering from its difficult start and reduce any incentive to consider a trade.

Denver represents a plausible theoretical destination, but there is currently no indication that Barkley is available or that the Broncos intend to pursue him.

articles.title: Jason Kelce ranks Eagles tailgate wedding just behind Travis and Taylor Swift’s big day
articles.standfirst: Jason helped create the memory of a lifetime for Lindsey Carl and Brandon Byrd
articles.summary: Jason helped create the memory of a lifetime for Lindsey Carl and Brandon Byrd
articles.body:
J ason Kelce has witnessed two very different wedding celebrations this year, from his brother Travis ’ star-studded ceremony with Taylor Swift to a Philadelphia Eagles -themed marriage held outside Lincoln Financial Field . The former center had a clear favorite, although he later revised his ranking after Lindsey Carl and Brandon Byrd won a competition organized by Garage Beer , the brand associated with the NFL brothers.

Earning the chance to exchange vows in the Eagles ’ parking lot before the game against the Dallas Cowboys , Jason attended the ceremony and later reflected on the occasion during ESPN 's Monday Night Countdown . And he described it as an unforgettable gathering, joking that it was probably the most legendary wedding he had attended all year as host Scott Van Pelt , who attended Travis and Swift ’s wedding over the summer, challenged the claim. But the one-time Super Bowl winner laughed before conceding that he might have been too generous with his initial assessment, ultimately placing the tailgate celebration second. The newlyweds embraced Philadelphia ’s football culture throughout the event whilst Carl wore a traditional white wedding dress with Eagles cowboy boots, while Byrd chose a green suit, team-themed socks and a feather attached to his lapel. Their aisle was also green, matching the occasion’s colors as Carl walked alongside her father before the couple exchanged rings as the Philly Pops performed and former Philadelphia Phillies star Shane Victorino officiated the ceremony. After being pronounced husband and wife, the couple released white doves from a heart-shaped basket and Jason helped distribute cans of beer and congratulate the newlyweds, bringing the Garage Beer connection directly into the festivities.

Cowboys hand Eagles fifth straight loss on Monday Night Football

Whilst Carl and Byrd had a good time away from the field, on it there was little joy to discover as the Cowboys kept their NFC East hopes alive with a 38-21 victory over the Eagles . Dak Prescott threw for 212 yards and three touchdowns, including two to CeeDee Lamb , whilst Javonte Williams rushed for a career-high 155 yards and another score. Philadelphia led 21-20 in the third quarter after backup quarterback Tanner McKee found Makai Lemon for a four-yard touchdown, capping a drive that consumed almost 10 minutes. Dallas responded when Prescott connected with Lamb on a 16-yard touchdown before running in the two-point conversion to restore the Cowboys ' advantage. Brandon Aubrey added three field goals, and Williams scored from two yards out to complete the victory. Dallas finished with 204 rushing yards, while the Eagles surrendered 416 total yards and 25 first downs. McKee completed 23 of 35 passes for 211 yards, one touchdown and one interception as he steps in for the injured Jalen Hurts , who is managing a serious blood clot issue and is out for the year. The Eagles fell to 2-5, their longest losing streak since 2016 and effectively see their hopes of reaching the NFL Playoffs end – a shocking slump for a side that won the Super Bowl in February 2025.

articles.title: The strict rule Kylie and Jason Kelce imposed on parents with their children: "No kissing"
articles.standfirst: Kylie revealed the boundary she established with her and Jason Kelce’s parents when they welcomed their first daughter
articles.summary: Kylie revealed the boundary she established with her and Jason Kelce’s parents when they welcomed their first daughter
articles.body:
Kylie Kelce has opened up about one of the first parenting rules she introduced after becoming a mother, revealing that she asked relatives not to kiss her newborn daughter on the face, head or hands.

The 34-year-old podcaster, who shares four daughters with former Philadelphia Eagles star Jason Kelce , discussed the subject during a question-and-answer segment in a bonus clip of her Not Gonna Lie podcast.

Asked whether she had ever needed to establish boundaries with her own parents or her husband's parents, Kylie explained that one particular request had been straightforward to communicate.

“I asked people not to kiss her face or her head or her hands and everybody listened,” she said after thinking about the question for a brief moment. “We have a good little squad. Squad understands the assignment.”

Rather than describing a difficult family disagreement, Kylie portrayed the experience as a positive example of relatives respecting the decisions she and Jason made as new parents.

“[Our] squad is very respectful about the fact that they have raised their grown children and that this is an opportunity for them to be fun, loving grandparents and supportive,” Kylie continued. “We actually made out like thieves on this one.”

The grandparents accepted that the parents would determine how their children should be cared for. The rule also reflected the extra caution Kylie felt when her eldest daughter, Wyatt, was still a baby.

Pandemic made the couple more cautious

Kylie and Jason welcomed Wyatt in October 2019. When the COVID-19 pandemic began affecting everyday life in 2020, their daughter was around six months old, making health precautions an important consideration for the family.

Kylie explained that the uncertainty surrounding the virus, combined with her own concerns about germs, prompted them to take a careful approach.

“Being the germaphobe that I am and also the unknown with a six-month-old in your house, we locked it down pretty fast. We were very careful,” she explained. “That was the time where we set boundaries just in terms of like travel and things like that.”

“But outside of that, not really,” she added, referring to boundary setting in her family. “Everyone understands the assignment. So, we really lucked out.”

The experience appears to have helped establish a family dynamic in which Kylie and Jason could make decisions about their daughters while still relying on the support of their relatives.

The couple now have four children: Wyatt, seven, Elliotte, five, Bennett, three, and Finnley, who was around 18 months old when Kylie discussed the subject.

Their family life has attracted considerable public interest, particularly following Jason 's NFL career and the wider attention surrounding the Kelce family.

According to Us Weekly, Jason 's parents, Donna and Ed Kelce , have been involved in their grandchildren's lives, with Donna previously discussing the balance between showing affection and respecting the parents' decisions.

For Kylie , the ability to set expectations without creating tension has been an important part of that relationship. She described a family that has generally been receptive to her and Jason's approach.

Protecting the girls' privacy online

Physical boundaries are only one part of the couple's approach to parenting. Kylie has also spoken about becoming increasingly deliberate about how much of her daughters' lives she shares with the public.

During an appearance on Tay Lautner's The Squeeze podcast, she explained that the family's growing profile had changed how she viewed posting photographs of the children on social media.

“Life has gone on, and things have changed. I post infrequently overall, and I post even less frequently about our children,” she said. “I didn’t want to exclude them entirely, [but] I made it a point to stop putting their faces on my social media.”

Kylie said the release of Jason 's documentary marked a “turning point” in her thinking, as she became more conscious of the difficulty of maintaining a boundary between public interest and her children's private lives.

articles.title: The NFL forces Saquon Barkley to withdraw from new sports betting business venture
articles.standfirst: The Philadelphia running back has built an extensive investment portfolio
articles.summary: The Philadelphia running back has built an extensive investment portfolio
articles.body:
S aquon Barkley 's efforts to build a business empire beyond his NFL career have hit an unexpected obstacle, with the Philadelphia Eagles star revealing that league regulations forced him to abandon an investment in Polymarket.

The running back has become increasingly active in the investment world, acquiring stakes in technology companies and startups as he looks to establish financial opportunities beyond football.

However, his ownership interest in the prediction-market platform conflicted with the NFL's gambling policies.

Barkley confirmed to Front Office Sports that he previously invested in Polymarket but had to sell his shares after learning that players were prohibited from holding financial interests in prediction-market companies.

"I am not in that right now," Barkley said. "I am not allowed to be in that."

The 29-year-old explained that the NFL reviews permitted endorsements, investments and business relationships with players before each season, with the restrictions surrounding prediction markets becoming clear during that process.

"So I kinda had to get out of that," Barkley added.

The financial implications remain unknown, with neither the size of Barkley's original investment nor the amount he received for his stake publicly disclosed.

Why the NFL blocked Barkley's Polymarket ownership

The decision reflects the NFL's cautious approach toward prediction markets, which allow customers to trade contracts based on the outcomes of future events, including sporting contests.

Although Polymarket and rival Kalshi operate differently from conventional sportsbooks, the NFL applies its restrictions on gambling-related investments and endorsements to both companies.

NFL spokesman Brian McCarthy made the league's position clear earlier this year when asked whether its players could invest in prediction-market businesses.

"NFL players may not own a stake," McCarthy told NBC Sports.

That stance has created an increasingly noticeable divide between professional sports organizations. NBA superstar Giannis Antetokounmpo became an investor in Kalshi, while the basketball league has subsequently established commercial relationships with both major prediction-market platforms.

Major League Baseball, the NHL and Major League Soccer have also reached agreements with prediction-market companies, demonstrating how differently the industry is being approached across American sports.

The NFL has instead raised concerns about regulation and consumer protections, questioning whether sports-related prediction contracts should be governed under the same framework as traditional gambling.

Saquon Barkley's growing investment portfolio remains intact

Despite losing his Polymarket stake, Barkley has established an extensive collection of investments designed to generate income beyond his playing career.

His holdings have included financial technology company Ramp, where he pursued an ownership arrangement alongside an advertising appearance before Super Bowl LIX.

Barkley has also invested in Anthropic, Anduril, Neuralink, Cognition and Strike, reflecting his interest in emerging technologies and businesses with significant growth potential.

His investment strategy emphasizes acquiring equity rather than relying solely on conventional endorsement contracts, an approach that could provide financial benefits long after his NFL career concludes.

The forced Polymarket exit does not appear to have changed those ambitions, but it has exposed an important limitation facing NFL players seeking opportunities in the expanding sports prediction industry.

As rival leagues increasingly embrace the sector, Barkley's experience illustrates how the same investment can be permitted for one professional athlete while remaining prohibited for another.
